It introduces a temporal bird's-eye-view (BEV) architecture that combines multi-camera perception, HD-map information and route conditioning to predict future vehicle motion. The evaluated model uses a pretrained camera-BEV backbone, temporal feature fusion and a lightweight recurrent trajectory planner. It contains approximately 79.9 million parameters, of which approximately 1.45 million are trainable in the evaluated configuration. The v1.0 release provides model checkpoints, training and evaluation code, and DataModelConsole, a dashboard for visualizing and inspecting model experiments. On the KITScenes validation benchmark, the fine-tuned checkpoint achieves an average displacement error (ADE) of 0.745 m and a final displacement error (FDE) of 2.020 m at a three-second prediction horizon. The paper also reports preliminary real-vehicle research conducted with the Technical University of Munich's EDGAR platform, alongside ongoing collaboration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology. AutoE2E v1.0 is an early open research release. Its quantitative evaluation is open-loop, and the model has not yet demonstrated validated closed-loop autonomous driving. The release is intended to provide the autonomous-driving community with an inspectable baseline for further research, experimentation and collaborative development.

papers.title: NONSENSE: Non-Semantic Strings Expose Semanticity Gaps in Dense Retrieval
papers.abstract: Dense retrieval is central to modern search, question answering, and retrieval-augmented generation, where high similarity is often treated as evidence of semantic relevance. We stress-test this assumption with NONSENSE, a black-box optimization framework that constructs visibly non-semantic strings by optimizing only their dense similarity to the query. Across seven retrieval datasets and five single-vector retrievers, these strings frequently outscore the retriever's own best judged query-relevant passage (QRP) and often rank first in the full corpus. The result indicates a semanticity gap in the evaluated dense retrievers: strings with no coherent passage-level semantic content can lie closer to the query in embedding space than genuine relevant evidence. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating dense retrievers not only by whether they retrieve relevant documents, but also by whether their similarity scores reliably reflect semantic evidence.

papers.title: CueSplat: Learning to Schedule Sparse Deformation for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting on Edge Devices
papers.abstract: Deformation-based 4D Gaussian splatting (4DGS) enables dynamic scene rendering. However, evaluating deformation networks for all Gaussians at every frame is compute-intensive on edge devices. We find that Gaussian trajectories are often locally predictable, yet prediction reliability varies across Gaussians and time. Thus, we propose CueSplat, a post-training framework that exploits local temporal regularity while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen and retaining its Gaussian set. Specifically, CueSplat predicts Gaussian attributes from recent history and uses a lightweight learned router to select exact deformation updates within a scene-specific budget calibrated offline. Selection accounts for prediction reliability and rendering contribution. Selected indices are reused across nearby frames to reduce routing overhead, while selected Gaussians still receive exact updates each frame. To control accumulated prediction error, we use drift signals to schedule three consecutive full-deformation frames that rebuild the prediction history. Evaluated across four mainstream 4DGS algorithms, CueSplat achieves up to $6.74\times$ and $8.15\times$ speedups on Jetson AGX Orin and Orin NX, respectively, with a negligible quality drop (at most $0.16$ dB in dataset-average PSNR).

papers.title: Beyond Marginal Risk: ESG and Multidimensional Fragility in Equity Markets
papers.abstract: Do ESG characteristics provide financial resilience beyond conventional risk, and is that inference stable to the financial state and ESG score being measured? We study a point-in-time panel of nonfinancial S&P 500 constituents from January 2019 through November 2025. Once ex ante return, volatility, and liquidity exposures are modeled explicitly, the broad downside-resilience pattern attenuates and none of the three primary marginal ESG $\times$ Down tests survives Holm adjustment under either conventional or wild-cluster-bootstrap inference. A post-primary exact decomposition then shows that the negative Return+RVOL coefficient is almost entirely allocated to observations that also breach the CHL trading-cost tail, while the mutually exclusive Return+RVOL-only component is essentially zero. Finally, a paired standardized comparison on an identical sample shows that MSCI's downstream Industry Adjusted Score and upstream Weighted Average Key Issue Score imply materially different fitted associations in adverse market states: at a 5% market decline, the difference is about one probability percentage point per score standard deviation. Sector-time, leave- one-month-out, and observed-change timing diagnostics preserve most of this contrast, although the result remains exploratory and inference is sensitive to multiplicity and market-state support. The evidence therefore favors a narrower interpretation of ESG resilience: the apparent association weakens once conventional risk is modeled, while the remaining relation depends on both the adverse state and the MSCI score field used to represent ESG.

papers.title: FIDEL: Abugida-Aware Pre-tokenization for Ethiopic Languages
papers.abstract: Subword tokenizers assume that meaningful linguistic units can be recovered by splitting text at learned boundaries, an assumption better suited to concatenative morphology than to Semitic root-and-pattern systems. The challenge is acute for the Ethiopic languages, whose abugida script encodes consonant-vowel units as single characters and hides consonantal structure. We introduce FIDEL (FIdäl DEcomposition and Linearization), a family of reversible abugida-aware pre-tokenization schemes that expose consonant and vowel-order structure, extend SPLINTER reductions from abjad scripts to the Ethiopic abugida, and evaluate them on three Ethiopic languages under controlled conditions, holding corpus, architecture, budget and protocol fixed so that tokenization is the only variable. We report intrinsic tokenizer statistics for BPE and UnigramLM across vocabulary sizes alongside downstream NLP tasks, including transfer scenarios. We find that FIDEL reduction improves news classification consistently and named-entity recognition at larger capacity, while sentiment analysis performance declines under the more aggressive schemes, and extractive question answering performance is preserved.

papers.title: The Silent Cost of Conversation History in LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in multi-turn information systems accumulate their own earlier replies and a growing task state. We asked whether this conversation history lowers accuracy, and whether process-level quality metrics warn before it does. Each analysis was fixed before its outcomes were computed. In Study 1, on 48 sharded math tasks, retaining its replies lowered final success by 0.21 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.29 for Mistral-7B (Holm-adjusted p = 0.026 and 0.004); Llama-4 Scout showed the same direction, not significant. Study 2 introduces CDR-Stream, 100-turn state-tracking dialogues with an exact answer per turn and per-model difficulty calibration. With the full history, accuracy fell from about 0.6 to 0.1 within twenty turns at matched difficulty, whereas a solver-verified state summary kept it 0.52-0.59 higher (Holm-adjusted p less than 0.001). Consistency and logical coherence fell far less than accuracy, and stability rose. None of these metrics, a paired readiness measure or calibrated single-stream drift detectors gave robust, model-general early warning, although in Study 2 the repeat-based metrics were complete only for GPT-4o-mini. In the monitors we tested, a single 100-turn stream had power only for very large drops. Systems built on LLMs should keep task state outside the transcript and monitor across sessions.

papers.title: Improving fine-grained expressivity of graph neural networks
papers.abstract: This thesis investigates the expressive power of neural networks for structured data, focusing on graph neural networks and symmetry-aware architectures. We present four main contributions. First, we characterize the generic expressive power of geometric message-passing neural networks on sparse graphs and introduce EGenNet, an architecture achieving the corresponding guarantees. Second, we use representation theory to characterize linear layers equivariant to multiple permutations, including wreath-product symmetries. Third, we study permutation-invariant set representations that preserve containment, establish dimensional bounds and impossibility results, and introduce MASNet. Finally, we propose FSW-GNN, a message-passing architecture combining strong expressivity and bi-Lipschitz stability guarantees with strong empirical performance on long-range graph-learning tasks. Together, these results provide a broader understanding of how neural architectures can preserve the geometric, algebraic, order-theoretic, and metric structure of their inputs.

papers.title: HEmIF-Bench: Benchmarking H&E-to-mIF Models Beyond Virtual-Stain Fidelity
papers.abstract: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-to-multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) generators predict spatial protein expression from routine histology, yet pixel-level marker reconstruction does not establish downstream utility. We present HEmIF-Bench, evaluating five frozen generators across eight datasets spanning molecular, cellular, tissue, and patient scales. HEmIF-Bench decouples internal encoder features from generated outputs, benchmarking both against the pathology foundation reference UNI2. Mirroring the clinical workflow where pathologists rely on mIF to define cell phenotypes, delineate tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) and germinal centers (GCs), and stratify patient risk, we evaluate external CD3 recovery, single-cell classification, dense nuclear segmentation, TLS/GC segmentation, and patient survival prediction. Across the benchmark, foundation-model-based MIPHEI-ViT leads among the generators, while non-foundation models show task-specific strengths. Comparing the two routes reveals that internal encoder features generally outperform generated outputs, and larger output marker panels do not guarantee stronger downstream utility across datasets. Moreover, neither internal encoder features nor generated outputs consistently surpass frozen UNI2. These findings show that pixel-level stain fidelity does not equate to downstream utility, and that generators trained at current paired-data scales have yet to surpass large-scale pure-H&E foundation models. With the expansion of paired translation cohorts and the advancement of foundation-based generative architectures, HEmIF-Bench establishes a definitive benchmark for tracking when H&E-to-mIF generation crosses the threshold to deliver genuine value beyond routine histology for tumor microenvironment analysis and precision oncology.

papers.title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
papers.abstract: We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $κ_τ\Barψσ_{μν}F_{μν}ψ$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi (WT) identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$γ_A$. Consequently, at any fixed point with a vanishing gauge coupling, the eigenvalue in the direction of the gauge coupling is exactly~$-γ_A^*$, and the gauge coupling is relevant if and only if the vacuum polarization makes~$γ_A^*$ negative. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields such a fixed point, with~$γ_A^*=-1$ and three relevant directions. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line eliminate it unless $N_f$ is at least several tens. For~$N_f=1$, a search over the whole plane of the Pauli coupling and the mass parameter in the subspace~$e_τ=0$, where our flow equation is exactly of one-loop order, finds a single fixed point, at strong Pauli coupling and a finite mass parameter. Like one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell, it has a finite mass parameter and two relevant directions. At their fixed point, the gauge coupling is relevant. At ours, in contrast, $γ_A^*>0$, so that the gauge coupling is irrelevant, and the fixed point cannot provide a UV completion of QED with a nonzero charge. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$ on the critical surface connected to the Gaussian fixed point, $κ_τ$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value proportional to~$e_τ^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_τ^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.

papers.title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices
papers.abstract: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be $\le 1$ (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~$A_4$ lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~$A_6$ lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Type-3 New General Relativity on $Λ$CDM Background
papers.abstract: We investigate whether Type-3 New General Relativity can alleviate the cosmic growth tension. On a $Λ$CDM background, we derive the scalar perturbation equations and find the effective gravitational coupling to exceed Newton's constant throughout the parameter range compatible with ghost-free and background-hierarchy conditions. By confronting the theoretical model with growth-rate measurements from major galaxy redshift surveys, including WiggleZ, SDSS-IV eBOSS, BOSS, and VIPERS, we obtain constraints on the effective coupling that are consistent with the $Λ$CDM value. Consequently, the conditions for stability and tension reduction are mutually exclusive.

papers.title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
papers.abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.

papers.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
papers.abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.

papers.title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Experimental optimization of perovskite solar cells is constrained by combinatorial diversity in absorber compositions, device layers, and processing, which makes virtual screening attractive for prioritizing recipes before fabrication. We develop a surrogate-guided reinforcement-learning framework that casts recipe generation as virtual screening, enriching candidate shortlists near high-performing experimental neighbors. A frozen Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) guides recipe generation, while a reference pool of 890 measured devices enables neighborhood-based assessment. Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices shows top-ten selection raises mean power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 19.68\% to 23.74\%. Three learned policies are compared with six baselines under 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run. In top-100 shortlists, Proximal policy optimization (PPO) and recurrent PPO (RPPO) achieve neighborhood-supported hit rates of 23\% and 24\% (7.9- and 8.3-fold Pure Random's 2.9\%), versus 10\% (3.4-fold) for the baselines with the highest supported hit rate (L-SHADE and Ax BO, tied) at $K = 100$. Gains coexist with weak-support fractions. Of 9,000 recipes, 65.4\% match a composition family at similarity 0.80, falling to 11.7\% at 0.90. Results support enrichment-oriented prioritization but not experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage.

papers.title: Imitation Policies Learn a Proprioceptive Anchor: A Predictive Law for Perception Noise and Its Closed-Loop Cost
papers.abstract: Imitation policies for robot manipulation are often trained on noisy object positions, and they learn to discount the noisy reading. We show how much they discount it, and why. Because demonstrators steer toward the object, the robot's own state carries information about where the object is. A trained policy combines this proprioceptive anchor with the reading and weights the reading by $α= V/(V + s^2)$, where $s^2$ is the reading noise and $V$ the anchor's error variance. $V$ belongs to the learner and is far smaller than a linear model of the demonstrations implies, which is why classical errors-in-variables (EIV) regression overestimates $α$. Measured once, $V$ predicted ten held-out sensitivities across two robomimic tasks, two learners and four new noise levels, with mean absolute error 0.025 against 0.37 for classical EIV, and a parameter-free bias test rules out the simpler explanation that the policies just overestimate the noise. The discount does not carry over to deployment, where the policy produces its own state: closed-loop sensitivity to a persistent reading offset exceeded $α$ in all 15 policies that passed the registered gates, although the stricter registered prediction, that all would follow the offset fully, held for 8 of them. Post hoc, lower $α$ went with lower success, steeply for diffusion, and a registered prospective test confirmed this for diffusion on Can at two new noise levels: the measured $α$ predicted success before any rollout, within 0.03 (95% intervals $\pm 0.08$), although training noise predicts it equally well. Every test was registered before its data, including the classical benchmark that failed, and all other analyses are labelled post hoc; all results are in simulation with synthetic Gaussian noise.

papers.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$, answering the question of \cite{CLMP}. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.

papers.title: Where Is Uncertainty Observed? A Mechanistic Understanding of Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
papers.abstract: Knowing when a large language model's (LLM's) response can be trusted is critical for its safe use. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) can help LLMs recognize if their responses may be unreliable. Existing taxonomies organize UQ methods by uncertainty source or estimation mechanism. They leave unresolved the question of where uncertainty is observed in the model's computation. The answer matters because the observation point determines whether an estimator has access to enough information to recover a given target, and how well it can recover it. Drawing on mechanistic interpretability, we define four mechanistic observation lenses: the structural lens observes component updates, the representational lens observes hidden states, the distributional lens observes token probabilities, and the semantical lens observes distributions over meanings. We relate these lenses through the residual stream and order them by the information they carry, which gives a principle for selecting UQ methods for different targets. We survey existing methods through the four lenses. Furthermore, we distinguish evaluation targets, criteria, and metrics to clarify different UQ evaluation protocols. Finally, we identify open problems and research directions to connect uncertainty estimation to the internal computation and downstream use of LLMs.

papers.title: Multi-pump amplification of frequency-separated Stokes waves in stimulated Brillouin side scattering
papers.abstract: Multibeam stimulated Brillouin side scattering (SBSS) can be enhanced when one side-scattered light wave is amplified by several pump waves through different ion-acoustic waves (IAWs). This mechanism differs from models in which several pumps share the same scattered-light wave or the same IAW. Side-scattered light generated by different pumps can propagate in nearly the same direction but have different frequencies. We examine this process using a local temporal-growth calculation, a finite-width Gaussian k-space model, a three-dimensional envelope model, and two-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. These cross-beam three-wave interactions increase temporal growth and convective gain over the crossing angles considered. In the three-dimensional envelope calculations, direct SBS interactions alone produce weak, localized side scattering, whereas including the cross-beam interactions produces a strong response for the same incident fields and initial perturbations. The enhancement remains when the total incident power is fixed, so it comes from the cross-beam interactions rather than from extra laser power. The PIC simulations show stronger side scattering and several pump-specific IAWs, with a non-monotonic dependence on beam number. These results identify cross-beam amplification of frequency-separated side-scattered light as a gain pathway that should be considered when interpreting multibeam SBS experiments.

papers.title: $\varepsilon$-WM: Error-Driven Dynamics Adaptation across Fast--Slow Timescales for World Modeling
papers.abstract: A core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to balance three key requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, rapidly correcting sudden changes; stability, avoiding lasting model updates from transient disturbances; and persistence, retaining adapted dynamics during the observation-free open-loop rollout. Inspired by multi-timescale predictive coding in the human brain, we propose $\varepsilon$-WM, a world model that adapts to unknown dynamics through error-driven corrections across fast and slow timescales. $\varepsilon$-WM incorporates three novel features: 1) Multiple internal experts (MiE) emulate neural pathway reweighting, each combining a fixed base expert with fast--slow adaptation networks. 2) Fast--slow timescale adaptation captures distinct adaptation dynamics: fast states respond rapidly and decay, whereas slow states accumulate corrections and persist. 3) Predictive correction uses prediction errors to update fast and slow states and reweight experts without gradients. During open-loop rollout, each expert feeds back its own predictions, and $\varepsilon$-WM aggregates their outputs through adaptive weighting. Extensive experiments show $\varepsilon$-WM has a consistently lower multi-step mean error than all ten baselines on six datasets, verifying the effectiveness of each feature.

papers.title: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care
papers.abstract: Arterial, venous, pulmonary artery, and intracranial pressures and ventilator waveforms guide decisions in operating rooms and intensive care units, yet foundation models for physiological waveforms rely almost entirely on the electrocardiogram and photoplethysmogram. We present the CArdio-Respiratory Multi-modal ENcoder (CARMEN), a single encoder pretrained without labels on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms (2.27 million modality-hours). CARMEN accepts any combination of co-recorded signals at variable lengths. A conditioning mechanism, LSCNorm, restores the absolute signal level removed by normalization; in a matched ablation, replacing it with standard normalization lowered the AUROC for intraoperative hypotension by 0.11. Across 19 tasks from Korean and US cohorts, the frozen encoder significantly outperformed both supervised models in 12 of the 15 tasks on which they were evaluated. It outperformed three pretrained foundation models on 14--17 of 19 tasks, and none of them exceeded it on any task. Given the electrocardiogram or photoplethysmogram alone, it matched or exceeded the signal-specific foundation models in most comparisons, and the performance was largely preserved even after removing the secondary channels.

papers.title: A nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring with finitely based matrix semirings
papers.abstract: We establish that the matrix semiring $\mathbf{M}_n(SR_6)$ over the six-element nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring $SR_6$ is finitely based for every $n \geq 2$. This provides the first known example of an additively idempotent semiring $S$ that is nonfinitely based, while the matrix semirings $\mathbf{M}_n(S)$ are finitely based. Moreover, we show that the interval $[\mathsf{V}(SR_6), \mathsf{V}(\mathbf{M}_2(SR_6))]$ in the lattice of additively idempotent semiring varieties has the cardinality of the continuum.

papers.title: Mutual Linearity in Nonlinear Population Dynamics
papers.abstract: Mutual linearity, the persistence of affine relations among stationary observables under arbitrarily strong changes of one transition rate, is known for Markov jump processes and chemical reaction networks. We show that generalized Lotka--Volterra dynamics form a new class of mutually linear systems, even though species can go extinct and attractors can be chaotic. Any change to one species' equation acts on the others as one effective press and keeps all abundances affinely related: piecewise across extinctions, and as time averages on chaotic attractors.

papers.title: Emilia2: A Large-Scale Dataset for Controllable Long-Form Speech Generation
papers.abstract: Generating long-form speech requires models to keep content, speaker identity, turn-taking, and expressive style consistent over time. Yet most open training corpora contain examples lasting only tens of seconds and open long-form benchmarks cover at most two speakers per recording. We introduce Emilia2, a 229K-hour multilingual dataset for controllable long-form speech generation. From in-the-wild data, Emilia2 constructs short utterances, single-speaker long-form speech, and multi-speaker dialogues, preserving transcripts, speaker identities, pauses, and acoustic transitions. Examples longer than five minutes account for 50.0% of single-speaker long-form hours and 66.8% of dialogue hours. To support expressive control, Emilia2 provides natural language instructions for 4.77M examples and nonverbal-vocalization tags for 933K examples. We also introduce Emilia2-testset, 23 hours of bilingual recordings of up to 30 minutes and four speakers, each speaker paired with reference audio. We train autoregressive (AR) and non-autoregressive (NAR) models on Emilia2. Our 0.6B-backbone NAR model achieves the lowest Chinese CER and English WER on TTSD-Eval (5.27%/9.93%) among compared systems, while our AR model is on par with Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-VD on InstructTTSEval (zh/en: 76.2/78.3 vs. 77.1/77.9). These results validate Emilia2 as a comprehensive data foundation for long-form speech generation and minute-scale expressive control. Demo: https://charlesnii.github.io/Emilia2-demo/.

papers.title: The WoW: A Large-Scale World Knowledge Corpus for Full-Lifecycle LLM Training
papers.abstract: Existing Chinese educational corpora often suffer from fragmented coverage and a lack of systematic organization. In this paper, we propose WoW (\textbf{Wo}rld Kno\textbf{w}ledge), a large-scale dataset designed for the full-cycle training of foundation models. The construction of this dataset is driven by an Educational Knowledge Graph, which serves as a taxonomic backbone for the systematic collection and completion of missing educational modules across all levels. Compared to previous versions, this iteration provides enhanced systematicity, superior quality, and a larger scale, while incorporating multimodal signals and supporting every stage of model development. Experiments demonstrate that WoW significantly improves model performance across diverse benchmarks. To facilitate community research, we further provide an interactive platform for graph-based data selection and retrieval.

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, whose amplitudes are given by the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions whose shifts have power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, in which the slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed locally by matter and geometry without an external clock. This class includes the comoving and uniform-density gauges, whose spectra grow without bound at late times in radiation domination. Over this range of $w$, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, justifying its standard use in computing the gravitational-wave energy spectrum. In matter domination, by contrast, the out-state isolates the free wave from the static tidal response that asymptotically dominates the Newtonian-gauge tensor perturbation.

papers.title: Extending indoor airborne infection risk modelling to 3D, with local surface deposition
papers.abstract: Mathematical models of indoor disease transmission often rely on simplifying assumptions to reduce computational cost. In particular, in the Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS)[13], which combines architectural layout, people movement and airborne viral transmission, aerosol concentrations are assumed uniform across room height, allowing a two-dimensional (2D) formulation. Also, particle deposition on surfaces is represented by a first-order removal term acting throughout the computational domain. Here, we extend VIRIS to the VIRIS-3D-L framework to investigate how these two assumptions affect the predicted infection risk. In VIRIS-3D-L, we solve the reaction-diffusion equation in three dimensions (3D), and aerosol deposition is represented by local surface removal through a Robin boundary condition. We compare VIRIS with VIRIS-3D-L across three indoor settings of increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home, and a supermarket. For the courtroom, care home, and supermarket, respectively, at the end of the simulation, the original 2D formulation with global removal predicts average infection risks across individuals of 44%, 78%, and 25%, while VIRIS-3D-L predicts risks of 51%, 85%, and 28%. Thus, VIRIS significantly underestimates infection risk in all three settings. The predictions of VIRIS-3D-L also show agreement with a documented courtroom outbreak that was used to validate VIRIS. Although computation time increases by approximately a factor of four on average, simulations remain feasible on a standard laptop, taking between eight minutes and just under 1.5 hours. These findings suggest that VIRIS-3D-L offers a more physically realistic framework for assessing indoor airborne infection risk in indoor spaces without prohibitive computational costs.

papers.title: Stabilization of zero forcing numbers of finite quotients of periodic graphs
papers.abstract: We give a method for determining the zero forcing number of a graph by passing to an infinite cover. When the quotient map is a covering map, forcing commutes with taking preimages. If, in addition, the closure of every small set in the cover touches none of its translates, then no small set is a zero forcing set of the quotient. For covers that are periodic, this condition reduces to a property of the cover alone, and it gives an explicit threshold beyond which the zero forcing number of the quotient equals that of the cover. We apply the method to the generalized Petersen graphs: $Z(P(n,k))=2k+2$ for all $k\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2k^2+k+1$. We also show that the circulant $C_n(1,a)$ has zero forcing number $2a$ for all $n\ge 2a^2-a+1$.

papers.title: Computing EF1 Allocations under Budget Constraints in Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: We study the allocation of indivisible goods to agents with budgets and additive valuations. Each agent compares its bundle with every budget-feasible subset of another agent's bundle or of the unallocated goods. We give a strongly polynomial algorithm for computing an allocation that is envy-free up to one good (EF1), even when agents have different valuations and budgets. Deciding whether a given allocation satisfies EF1 is coNP-complete. Equivalently, deciding whether it violates EF1 is NP-complete. When all agents have the same valuation, we can compute an EF1 allocation with welfare at least $(1/2-\varepsilon)$ times the maximum feasible welfare in time polynomial in the input length and $1/\varepsilon$, for any $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Finding an allocation that is envy-free up to any good (EFX) is NP-hard even for one agent. We give polynomial-time EFX algorithms when each agent values goods in proportion to their sizes or when the number of distinct positive item values per agent is bounded by a constant.

papers.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis. While recent work in the visual domain has explored direct conditioning on brain activity, this approach has not yet been extended to audio diffusion models. We introduce MAAS (Multi-Area Auditory Synthesis), an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer on ROI-wise fMRI responses without first supervising a decoder to predict an external stimulus representation. MAAS uses region-specific projections and learned brain tokens to condition Stable Audio through a dedicated cross-attention pathway. On a 7T fMRI dataset, we demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines, including two-stage fMRI-to-latent conditioning, across both acoustic and semantic evaluation metrics. In addition, we introduce a fidelity metric grounded in a computational model of auditory neural processing, which allows us to quantify the contribution of individual auditory cortical regions to reconstructed audio representations.

papers.title: Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
papers.abstract: The Karhunen-Loève transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix, below 1.2 percent for the $8\times8$ Markov block at pole $0.95$. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra. A moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exactly for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows. The dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means. This version adds complex data on the cyclic group with a border departure of rank exactly $2p$, the mixed and integrated classes, odd-length cores, and a released implementation whose kernel evaluation counts are flat in $M\log_2(M/n_{\mathrm{leaf}})$ to 5.3 percent. Experiments on recorded acoustic-array, radar and vibration data state where the transform helps and where existing methods match it.

papers.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
papers.abstract: Given a graph $Γ$ with vertex set $V(Γ)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $Γ$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $Γ\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(Γ)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $Γ$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^Γ(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $Γ$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(Γ,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$, and show that they are log-concave. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.

papers.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
papers.abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is at least 2-dimensional. This strengthens the author's prior results to their optimal dimension bound and recovers Ebin's non-equivariant analogue to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

papers.title: The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential
papers.abstract: Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $α>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.

papers.title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics
papers.abstract: Video generation models can produce highly realistic videos while generating physically inconsistent object motion. This limitation suggests that visual modeling alone may not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics. We introduce MotionCore, a framework for learning physical dynamics via a learnable latent neural operator which focuses on rigid-body video generation. We introduce a latent neural simulator learning to predict the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion. Its predictions are then converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model. The generator serves as a visual interface: it provides appearance and scene detail, while the learned dynamics model specifies the physical trajectory. We construct our training dataset comprising semi-realistic synthetic multi-object videos with rich annotations. We evaluate MotionCore on public physical video generation benchmarks and conduct controlled ablations to assess the contribution of learned dynamics relative to other priors. Results indicate that MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings, while maintaining comparable visual quality. MotionCore outperforms larger general and physics-aware video generators while using substantially fewer parameters.

papers.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
papers.abstract: Repetition-code tomography compares a code's logical channel with a reference through a decoder, almost always standard minimum-weight. We ask how many single-qubit Pauli gates it needs with the measurement basis fixed---the constraint that makes the count a resource. Exhaustive enumeration at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$, ranks decided in exact arithmetic, gives minima of $0$, $1$ and $5$ gates, against $6$, $10$ and $14$ for first-order and $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full decoding. The count depends only on how many sites are corrected, not which, so it splits into a budget and a placement that decides identifiability; more sites is not monotonically better: at $n=7$ full decoding has rank $24$ of $27$, and the $n=3$ precision curve is U-shaped under a calibration floor. The three-gate design is $9.0$ times more precise than the standard six-gate decoder at the median of $40$ working points and better at every one, by $1.8$ to $88$-fold; fixing the placement in advance gives $6.9$, or $3.1$ for a pre-commitment never worse. Two certified placements lose no direction either sees and reach $10$\,mrad within twice the shots wherever identifiable. Measuring the reference everywhere gives a $16(n+2)$-component map, full rank at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$ with no gate and $44$ to $93\%$ fewer settings, though at $n=5$ and $7$ its floor stays one and three orders above target. The optima are not covariant under chain reversal.

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Resolution of Luttinger's Theorem Violations in Strongly Correlated Systems
papers.abstract: Many-body physics faces an apparent paradox concerning violations of Luttinger's theorem in strongly correlated systems. The theorem relates the electron number to the Luttinger count---the monodromy of the logarithm of the imaginary-frequency Green's function $\bd{G(iε)}$---and, at finite magnetic field, connects the Hall conductivity to the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger count via the Streda formula. Luttinger's theorem seemingly follows from particle-number conservation alone, without resorting to perturbation theory, and yet it is found to be violated. Here, we provide a non-perturbative solution to this paradox. We show that the Luttinger integral, which accounts for the mismatch between the particle number and the Luttinger count, is a pure zero-frequency boundary term, which the conventional proof implicitly discards. Hence, violations of Luttinger's theorem do not require a breakdown of the skeleton-diagram formalism, whose validity is independent of the convergence of the skeleton-diagram expansion to the exact solution. This advancement in understanding resolves a longstanding point of contention in many-body theory. We also find that the Luttinger integral is a genuine topological invariant, tied to the Luttinger-Ward functional rather than to the Green's function alone; like the monodromy of $\bd{\ln G(iε)}$, it stems exclusively from the zero-frequency point where the Matsubara trajectory crosses the branch cut of the logarithm. Correspondingly, the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger integral makes the Hall number in topological insulators differ from its Green's-function expression by a vertex correction, itself invariant, which can take fractional values.

papers.title: On bordism classes of symmetric products of surfaces
papers.abstract: We explicitly determine the complex bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a complex curve of genus $g$. In particular, we provide an explicit formula expressing this class as an integral linear combination of bordism classes of products of complex projective spaces. Similarly, we determine the unoriented bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a non-orientable surface of genus $g$ (i.e., $\#_{i=1}^{g+1}\mathbb R P^2$). It turns out that these classes are also expressed as a $\mathbb Z_2$-linear combination of bordism classes of products of even-dimensional real projective spaces. We also give an affirmative answer to a non-orientable version of the Blagojević--Grujić--Živaljević conjecture stating that the topological type of any symmetric product of a noncompact surface of finite type determines the topological type of the surface itself.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of EDMA-NOMA Enhanced V-SWAN-Assisted ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a vertical segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (V-SWAN)-assisted downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) environmental division multiple access (EDMA) framework for simultaneously supporting multi-user communication and target sensing. In the proposed framework, multiple pinching antennas (PAs) are deployed along a segmented vertical dielectric waveguide to serve communication users (CUs), aerial users (AUs), and sensing target (ST). CUs are distributed on the ground, whereas AUs and ST are above the ground, where line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation conditions coexist. In particular, SWAN provides an effective platform for realizing EDMA by reducing the effective propagation distance and in-waveguide attenuation, thereby suppressing co-channel interference and enabling efficient multi-user transmission. The communication and sensing model are formulated, followed by the corresponding SINR expressions. We formulate the statistical characterizations for the combination of LoS and NLoS propagation for CUs, and LoS propagation for AUs and sensing channels for generalized multi-user, multi-PA scenarios. Based on these statistical characterizations, the segment outage and sensing outage probabilities are derived and evaluated for the generalized framework. The results show that the proposed framework outperforms the conventional H-SWAN and single vertical pinching antenna system (V-PASS) in terms of segment outage probability, sensing outage probability, and segment sum rate. Monte Carlo simulation results closely match the analytical results, validating the accuracy of the derived expressions. The results further highlight the impact of different system parameters on the performance of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Hidden Triakontadipole Order in the Triangular-Lattice Magnet CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$
papers.abstract: The absence of magnetic Bragg peaks and a broad excitation continuum are commonly recognized experimental features of a quantum spin liquid. The Ce-based triangular-lattice hexaaluminate CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$ exhibits both signatures, yet its effective model and ground state remain under debate. Experiments have variously suggested a quantum spin liquid, proximate umbrella point, and disorder-suppressed magnetic order. Here we trace these contradictions to an overlooked multipolar degree of freedom, and establish a dipole--triakontadipole XXZ model with $J_{\perp} \simeq 0.65$ K and $J_c \simeq -0.13$ K via precision tensor-network calculations. The resulting planar triakontadipolar superfluid order is hidden from dipolar probes, explaining the absence of a magnetic Bragg peak in neutron scattering. The zero-field excitations separate into a low-energy triakontadipole wave and a broad higher-energy continuum. We further propose nuclear spin-lattice relaxation and spin-current experiments to probe the gapless excitations of this hidden triakontadipole superfluid. Our findings thus offer a hidden-order caveat for spin-liquid searches and provide a new platform for exploring high-rank multipolar physics in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets.

papers.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds
papers.abstract: Video games provide a practical setting for collecting vision-language-action (VLA) data, whose acquisition in physical environments is costly. Existing datasets, however, remain limited by restricted game coverage, sparse language supervision, or temporal hierarchies that do not necessarily reflect changes in task objectives. We introduce AceAction, a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games for learning skill composition and subgoal transitions. AceAction organizes demonstrations around complete tasks, linking overall instructions, ordered subgoals, and local skill instructions to temporally aligned visual observations and keyboard-and-mouse actions. To construct these annotations, we develop a vision-language model pipeline that identifies subgoals from changes in objectives or interaction targets, anchors navigation goals to visually recognizable waypoints, and composes adjacent subgoals into task instructions. The resulting demonstrations cover navigation, reconnaissance, combat, interaction, and recovery, with explicit stage boundaries that connect task progression to fine-grained control. We assess annotation quality through model-based verification and human inspection. An audit of 500 trajectories yields a 95.8% pass rate across independent reviewer assessments. AceAction provides a data foundation for studying how agents execute, combine, and switch skills to follow complex instructions in dynamic game environments.

papers.title: Beyond the Federer paradox in tennis
papers.abstract: Roger Federer won about 80% of his professional matches with only 54% of the points. Hierarchical scoring amplifies small advantages on points into large advantages on matches, but also allows a player to win with fewer points than the opponent. Using Monte Carlo simulations and exact Markov chain calculations, we show that in tennis, badminton, volleyball and table tennis this amplification is set almost entirely by the number of points per match. We then let a player win ordinary points with probability p1 and crucial points, those closing a game, set or match, with probability p2. In every sport a narrow region of the (p1, p2) plane exists where a player wins most matches with fewer than half of the points, because crucial points carry more influence than their share of points. Of ATP matches played in 1991-2025, 4.7% were won with fewer points, 16% more than independent points predict (5% including the serve), a constant excess. Pressure performance measured in other seasons predicts match outcomes beyond the points won, and Fabio Fognini won 51% of his matches with 49% of the points, in what we call the Fognini paradox.

papers.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
papers.abstract: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.

papers.title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
papers.abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number $\ucr{K_n}$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is $Z(n):=\frac{1}{4}\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\rfloor$ for all $n\ge 3$. In October 2026 OpenAI uploaded to GitHub a proof of this conjecture. The proof is very short, but it relies on polynomial methods that are not part of the standard techniques used by many combinatorialists, and it is written with very little motivation or explanation. Since we found the proof very hard to follow, we decided to write this paper, which contains a complete proof of the conjecture written for mathematicians who are more familiar with combinatorics than with polynomial methods. In fact we prove a more general result on rotation systems of $K_n$, from which the Harary--Hill conjecture easily follows. Namely, we show that for every rotation system $Π$ of $K_n$ the number of $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$ realizable as drawings of $K_4$ with one crossing, plus three times the number of non-realizable $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$, is at least $Z(n)$. The statement and proof of our result are purely combinatorial and do not involve drawings at all.

papers.title: Can You Predict the Next Mind in the Symphony? Toward Multi-Turn Multi-Party Mental World Modeling
papers.abstract: Although multimodal foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in modeling, generation, and embodied reasoning in the physical world, their capacity for modeling the dynamic mental world remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks predominantly focus on static mental state perception or single-turn behavioral reasoning, overlooking the dynamic mental transitions of the observed individuals in multi-party, multi-turn interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce M$^3$WME-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate mental world modeling conditioned on evolving actions of interactants. Specifically, models are tasked with forecasting a target subject's future mental states and behaviors over extended social interactions. In addition to the benchmark suite, we construct M$^3$WME-23K, a dedicated training dataset, and establish a competitive baseline named MindNext-7B. Extensive evaluations across four representative paradigms (general MLLMs, emotion-specialized MLLMs, agentic frameworks, and World Foundation Models) reveal that current systems consistently struggle to anticipate forward-looking mental states. Mechanistic analyses further reveal that existing architectures fundamentally lack forward mental state transition dynamics. Our findings highlight a pivotal challenge in advancing agents from physical to mental world modeling, charting new directions for socially adaptive AI.

papers.title: MERIDIAN: Memory-Encoded Rituals for Intimacy across Distance in an Interactive, Asynchronous Neighbourhood
papers.abstract: How can shared memories become playable structures for partners who live in different time zones, and what becomes of such a gift once it is in use? We present MERIDIAN, a design case of Yi Town, a bilingual browser game developed by one member of a long-distance couple as a gift for the other. Nine levels translate personally meaningful events, places and cultural references into tasks within a navigable pixel town, framed by a birthday prologue and a fictional wedding. This second version extends the record by four weeks. Drawing on research through design, we reconstruct seven design changes from 152 commits, 36 changelog versions and four design specifications. In those weeks the site gained three products that are not levels: an infirmary for the days after a quarrel, which began with a remark by the recipient; a page for her booked flight, which replaces a symbolic ticket with a real one; and a request box whose messages are answered, while the designer sleeps, by a pipeline of a local language model and a hosted one. The request box ends the first version's claim of no author-operated backend, and we trace where her files now travel. An audit reproduced 263 passing unit tests; the progress model is unchanged and keeps its exhaustive check of 1,024 codes. The answering pipeline was tested in parts, and it began to receive real requests on the night it was built. No recipient evaluation or relationship outcome is reported. The contribution is an inspectable account of design decisions and their trade-offs: between authoring a gift and leaving the recipient free to decline or reshape it, and between being reachable across thirteen hours and answering in person. The site is at https://jingyifan.love and its source is public at https://github.com/rayford295/yi-town.

papers.title: Bulk gap stability and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions
papers.abstract: We prove that weak long-range many-body interactions preserve the bulk gap of a free fermion system and that a quasi-local spectral flow transports the free ground state to ground states of the interacting system. Let $Φ_h$ be a free fermionic interaction, possibly including pairing terms, whose infinite-volume Majorana coefficient operator $h$ has no spectrum in $(-g,g)$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an even self-adjoint many-body interaction. For sufficiently small $|λ|$, we construct pure ground states $ω_λ$ of the interacting bulk system $Φ_λ=Φ_h+λ\mathcal V$ and quasi-local automorphisms $β_{0,λ}$ such that $ω_λ=ω_0\circβ_{0,λ}$, where $ω_0$ is the free ground state of $Φ_h$. Each $ω_λ$ has a GNS Hamiltonian with gap at least $g-C_*|λ| \|\mathcal V\|_*$, where $\|\cdot\|_*$ is the relevant interaction norm. Our result allows polynomial decay of both the free coefficients and the many-body interaction. For two-site interactions on a uniformly discrete point set $Γ\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, a sufficient condition is decay as $(1+|x-y|)^{-\varpi}$ with $\varpi>2d$, for both the hopping and pairing coefficients and the interaction terms. The spectral-flow generator preserves the spatial exponent of the polynomial interaction norm, and its automorphisms satisfy locality bounds at that exponent. If $h$ and $\mathcal V$ have stretched-exponential decay, so does the spectral-flow generator. The proof constructs the spectral flow and establishes the gap through an excitation-number comparison, using polynomial propagation bounds for evolved interactions proved in a companion paper.

papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Adversarial Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses Across Seven Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) deployed in safety-critical settings must withstand adversarial inputs designed to elicit harmful outputs. This study systematically evaluates five jailbreak attack families-direct requests, roleplay, hypothetical framing, instruction override, and obfuscation-across seven locally served open-weight LLMs: Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma2-9B, and Phi-4-14B. We also assess four defense mechanisms-keyword blacklisting, self-reminder prompting, paraphrase-based sanitization, and perplexity-based filtering-on Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B using a 20-prompt subset. Across 250 prompts per model, obfuscation achieved the highest pooled success rate (62.3%) when HARMFUL and PARTIAL responses were counted, although only 7.1% were rated HARMFUL. Hypothetical framing was the most successful attack family for three models, while obfuscation achieved nonzero success across all seven. However, the content judge remains unvalidated against human labels, and preliminary non-expert assessment indicated substantially lower harm rates; therefore, these findings are provisional. Model size was not a significant predictor of robustness (Spearman Rho = -0.64, p = 0.12, n = 7). Notably, the content judge found little difference between Llama-3 generations (17.2% vs. 18.4%), unlike the rule-based judge (16.8% vs. 40.8%). Self-reminder prompting showed the largest defense improvement, reducing attack success rates from 50% to 10% on Mistral-7B and from 45% to 5% on Llama-3.1-8B. These 40-percentage-point reductions were measured against matched no-defense runs using a rule-based judge with known limitations, making the results provisional. Code and prompts are publicly available at https://github.com/Mdniloykhan/jailbreak-eval-7llms, while model responses and judge outputs are available upon request.

papers.title: Kairos: Fast and Reliable Symbolic Task Planning for Autonomous Robots
papers.abstract: Robots that plan while they act need a task planner that reads the models their designers write, answers within milliseconds, and says what each answer means. Models are written in the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), which has grown from classical planning to durative actions, numeric resources, time windows and continuous change, while planners cover one fragment each and differ in what their failures mean. The contribution in artificial intelligence is Kairos, a single planner, not a portfolio of existing planners, that covers the whole language and derives what each answer guarantees from the search that produced it. We prove when the exhaustion of a search shows that no plan exists, and give a relaxation of temporal tasks that proves unsolvability where temporal search cannot. For the compression of durative actions, we give a criterion on the values that actions read, prove that compression is sound, and show that it is not complete, so its failure is never reported as a proof. An independent validator checks every plan. The engineering application is on-line task planning for robots: Kairos is open source, packaged for the Robot Operating System, and the default planner of a widely used planning framework. On 1,756 public tasks from nine suites, Kairos solves more tasks than the strongest evaluated planner of each suite within 100 milliseconds, 1 second and 30 seconds; it proves ten of eleven unsolvable tasks, and handles each of the seventeen language features probed, where no other planner handles more than eight.

papers.title: An $L^p$ Version of Raeburn's Symmetric Imprimitivity Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $1\leq p<\infty$. We prove an $L^p$-operator analogue of Raeburn's symmetric imprimitivity theorem for countable discrete groups. Let $A$ be an $L^p$-operator algebra with a contractive two-sided approximate identity, admitting a nondegenerate isometric representation on a $σ$-finite $L^p$-space. Given commuting free and proper actions of groups $G$ and $H$ on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $Z$, together with commuting isometric actions on $A$, we show that the two corresponding full crossed products, and likewise the two reduced crossed products, are Morita equivalent as Banach algebras. The proof is organized through the linking groupoid. Its main analytic ingredient is a coefficient-valued spatial matrix dilation; in the reduced case we prove that this dilation preserves regularity after a Borel reindexing of the opposite corner. A pairing-valued approximate identity yields fullness and nondegeneracy.

papers.title: Martingale-Based Resource Partitioning Bounds for URLLC and eMBB Network Slicing in 5G
papers.abstract: Network slicing enables the coexistence of ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC) and enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) in 5G networks. However, provisioning limited radio resources under stochastic traffic and wireless service while satisfying heterogeneous quality-of-service (QoS) requirements remains challenging. This paper proposes a martingale-based resource block (RB) allocation framework for coexisting URLLC and eMBB slices. Under the stated independence assumptions, exponential martingales are constructed using the moment generating functions of the arrival and service processes. By applying Doob's maximal inequality, we derive analytical upper bounds on the URLLC virtual-delay violation probability and the eMBB backlog violation probability. These bounds provide sufficient QoS conditions for resource allocation. A bisection procedure determines the martingale parameters, followed by an integer search for the minimum RB allocations certified by the derived bounds. Numerical results show that the proposed bounds are tighter than an optimized Chernoff--union baseline in the evaluated scenario.

papers.title: safeL4: Rethinking Safe-Language-Based Single Address Space Microkernels
papers.abstract: Microkernels provide good features such as high security, safety, and flexibility, but their reliance on hardware-based isolation leads to heavy performance overhead, limiting their widespread adoption. Although constructing single-address-space microkernels based on safe language-based isolation is a promising approach to addressing the performance issue, this approach still faces challenges in maintaining the principle of minimality and enforcing capability-based, fine-grained access control over system resources. We propose safeL4, an approach to constructing microkernels based on safe languages. It guarantees minimality through low-level abstractions for unsafe operations, and implements a capability system based on the safe language's object capabilities to achieve fine-grained access control over all operations on system resources. We implement a prototype system in Rust, and our evaluation results show that the primitives provided by safeL4 are, on average, 1.9$\times$ faster than those of seL4.

papers.title: Scale-Dependent Statistics of Coherent Magnetic Structures in Early IMAP Observations
papers.abstract: We analyze early Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) magnetic field observations (November 2025 to May 2026) to quantify the statistical properties of helical magnetic structures and their relationship with turbulence intermittency. Intermittent structures, such as current sheets, are identified using the Partial Variance of Increments (PVI) method, and the scale-dependent normalized magnetic helicity is computed over scales corresponding to 0.5-3 correlation lengths. Prior studies have typically applied the PVI-helicity method to individual events; here we extend this technique to the ensemble statistics of a multi-month sample spanning many correlation times. To separate coherent helical structures from random turbulent fluctuations, significance thresholds for helicity are determined using phase-randomized surrogate realizations. We find a clear scale dependence in the occurrence, duration, and waiting time of coherent magnetic helicity, reminiscent of the scale-transfer arguments underlying inverse cascade, selective decay, and Taylor relaxation theories. Event duration and waiting-time distributions are well described by power-law and exponential models over different ranges, consistent with previous findings. In addition, PVI and magnetic helicity are anticorrelated, suggesting that high-PVI regions are preferentially associated with the boundaries of flux ropes, while their interiors tend to exhibit lower PVI and stronger magnetic helicity.

papers.title: OVM-Occ: Open-Vocabulary Monocular Occupancy Prediction via Geometry-Aware Vision-Language Distillation
papers.abstract: Monocular occupancy prediction in indoor scenes aims to recover a scene's 3D geometry and semantics from a single RGB image. Existing methods are restricted to a closed set of predefined categories, limiting their ability to generalize to unseen categories. This limitation is particularly critical in indoor scenes, where objects exhibit highly diverse and fine-grained semantic categories. We study open-vocabulary monocular occupancy prediction for indoor scenes and present OVM-Occ, a Gaussian-based occupancy framework with an instance-aware vision-language teacher. Specifically, we adopt Language-Embedded Gaussians as the intermediate scene representation, propose a geometry-aware deformable attention module to refine Gaussian semantic features, and construct instance-level vision-language embeddings to provide reliable semantic supervision. We further introduce geometry-aware decoupled semantic distillation to mitigate the interference between geometry learning and semantic learning. To evaluate open-vocabulary occupancy prediction performance, we introduce OpenOcc-ScanNet and OpenOcc-Replica, two extended benchmarks with more diverse and fine-grained semantic categories. Experiments show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in open-vocabulary monocular occupancy prediction for indoor scenes, outperforming the previous state-of-the-art approach by 12.2 mIoU and 0.6 IoU on the Occ-ScanNet dataset, with consistent gains under new open-vocabulary evaluation protocols.

papers.title: InterQ-RL: Interaction-Aware Correction of Execution Mismatch in Quantized Agentic RL
papers.abstract: Multi-turn agent reinforcement learning (RL) relies on long closed-loop rollouts, making generation and KV-cache costs a major bottleneck. Quantized rollout reduces these costs, but its low-precision executor also serves as the behavior policy and can induce execution mismatch with the learner. Existing quantized-RL methods are designed primarily for single-turn generation. They align the learner forward with quantized rollout or correct the current-token rollout-learner ratio, without modeling the policy history that produces each agent state. Even after quantization alignment, residual rollout-learner mismatch accumulates along the state-reaching policy history, so a current action may look locally aligned despite a mismatched history. We introduce InterQ-RL (Interaction-aware Quantized Reinforcement Learning) to correct this post-alignment mismatch. It applies bounded execution-prefix correction over the state-reaching policy history, allocates correction strength across action segments by effective support under a fixed displacement budget, and requires no additional model forward pass. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) backbones from 4B to 30B on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld, with all quantized arms sharing the same rollout with 8-bit weights, activations, and KV cache (W8A8-KV8). Across four environment-backbone settings, InterQ-RL achieves the strongest quantized endpoint result, matching BF16 to within 0.7 points and exceeding it in two settings. It matches or exceeds the learning speed of alignment alone while avoiding its late performance regression.

papers.title: Best Policy Tracking in Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning commonly exhibits non-monotonic performance dynamics in single-task settings. During learning, a sequence of policies is generated whose true performance is unknown and may oscillate significantly across iterations. Despite this well-known phenomenon, standard experimental practice typically reports either the final visited policy or the best among periodically evaluated ones, implicitly assuming that these selection criteria reliably approximate the best-performing policy visited throughout the entire sequence. In this work, we present an empirical study on the implications of non-monotonicity for policy selection in single-task policy-based reinforcement learning. We introduce post-hoc diagnostic metrics to characterize performance degradation and assess the accuracy and efficiency of different selection criteria. These metrics allow us to evaluate commonly used selection strategies across standard continuous-control benchmarks using a well-established on-policy actor-critic method. Our results show that, in this representative experimental setting, widely adopted selection practices can deviate considerably from the best policy encountered during learning, leading to underperforming estimates and suboptimal use of computational resources. As an alternative, we recommend a validation-based policy selection strategy constrained by computational cost, which provides a more consistent and accurate approximation of the best visited policy while improving selection efficiency. Overall, our findings highlight policy selection as an underexplored factor in the evaluation protocols of reinforcement learning and motivate further study on explicit and standardized validation-based selection procedures.

papers.title: A simple construction of smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carathéodory conjectures
papers.abstract: In a recent announcement, Alpöge presented smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carathéodory conjectures and credited John-Paul Smith. We present a simpler construction of a seed by using trigonometric functions. Using this, for every positive integer $k$, we construct a smooth real-valued function on the plane, flat at the origin, whose Hessian eigenline fields share the origin as an isolated singularity of index $1+k/2$. A support-function parametrization realizes this index as an umbilic index of a non-real-analytic $C^\infty$-regular surface germ in Euclidean $3$-space. The same framework, applied to a rapidly decreasing function on the whole plane, gives a strictly convex closed regular surface with exactly one umbilic, of index $2$. This paper is self-contained with regard to the existence of an isolated umbilic of index $2$ and the construction of a counterexample to the Carathéodory conjecture.

papers.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
papers.abstract: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$.
