A comprehensive simulation study, conducted over a range of sample sizes and noise levels, shows that the mean integrated squared error of the coefficient function decreases with more measurements per unit and that the SIMEX-extrapolated estimates achieve lower bias than the naive estimates based on the full set of measurements. The practical utility of the method is further illustrated through an application to the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, for which we relate 24-hour physical activity profiles to all-cause mortality. This example supports the validity of the method and demonstrates its ability to detect and correct for finite-measurement bias.

papers.title: SparDA: Sparse Decoupled Attention for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Sparse attention reduces compute and memory bandwidth for long-context LLM inference. However, two key challenges remain: (1) KV cache capacity still grows with sequence length, and offloading to CPU memory introduces a PCIe transfer bottleneck; (2) sparse selection during prefill retains $O(T^2)$ complexity and can dominate attention cost at long contexts. We propose SparDA, a decoupled sparse attention architecture that introduces a fourth per-layer projection, the Forecast, alongside Query, Key, and Value. The Forecast predicts the KV blocks needed by the next layer, enabling lookahead selection that overlaps CPU-to-GPU prefetch with current-layer execution. Because Forecast is decoupled from the attention query, our GQA implementation uses one Forecast head per GQA group, reducing selection overhead versus the original multi-head selector. On the evaluated 8B models, SparDA adds <0.5% parameters and trains only the Forecast projections using attention-derived supervision from the frozen backbone. On two sparse-pretrained 8B models, SparDA maintains accuracy comparable to the full-query sparse-attention baseline while delivering up to 1.25$\times$ prefill speedup and 1.7$\times$ decode speedup over the sparse-attention offload baseline. By enabling larger feasible batch sizes on a single GPU, SparDA further reaches up to 5.3$\times$ higher decode throughput than the non-offload sparse baseline on MiniCPM4.1-8B. Our adaptation to GLM-5.1 (754B MoE) also achieves accuracy comparable to native token-level DSA, extending the accuracy evaluation beyond block-sparse 8B models. Our source code is available at https://github.com/NVlabs/SparDA.

papers.title: Incremental SVD for Large-Scale Dynamic Matrices: Accuracy, Subspace Stability, Refresh Strategies, and Financial Factor-Based Risk Models
papers.abstract: Return panels, covariances, and large feature matrices evolve one observation or entry at a time, yet downstream models require an up-to-date low-rank factorization $A_t \approx U_t Σ_t V_t^\top$ on every tick - a regime where a full singular value decomposition (SVD) is prohibitive and existing alternatives sacrifice singular vectors, singular values, or long-horizon stability. We present a metric-driven study of Brand-style incremental SVD, built around a unified engine that handles row appends, column appends, rank-1 entry updates, and metrics tracking. For rank-1 entry updates, we derive an explicit projection-based rule $U'Σ'(V')^\top = P_U(\widehat{A} + δ\,e_ie_j^\top)P_V$ that keeps rank fixed while discarding only the out-of-subspace remainder quantifiably, turning Brand's rank-suppression heuristic into an operational scheme. Each update discards a part whose norm is available at negligible cost; the error at the last refresh plus the sum of these norms since then is an a posteriori error bound $β_t$. We then treat refresh scheduling as a first-class design axis, comparing periodic refresh with a bound-triggered rule that refreshes once $β_t/\|A_t\|_F$ exceeds a tolerance. The engine tracks error ratios, principal angles, explained variance, and per-update runtime on long synthetic streams and a factor model of exchange-traded funds for covariance and portfolio-risk estimation. With a sensible rank and refresh cadence, incremental SVD matches full-SVD accuracy within a few percent at a fraction of the cost. The bound-triggered rule keeps the relative error below any tolerance above its rank-$k$ optimum, with accuracy close to periodic refresh at a matched number of full SVDs.

papers.title: Human-Centered Learning Mechanics: Observable Entropy Control under Protected-Risk Constraints
papers.abstract: Human-Centered Learning Mechanics (HCLM) treats learning as an open, controlled process in which task progress, representation information, structural restrictions and externally specified risk limits jointly govern parameter updates. We characterise this mechanism through a normalised covariance-information force, metric observability and exact feasible rate constraints. The projected task rate depends on an observable cross-product that differs from the ordinary task information product when a probe set does not contain the training task. Error, finite-step and delay margins specify when admissible local requests can be implemented. A primary 288-run neural study separates information control from empirical risk protection and retains cases where extra compression worsens held-out loss. Follow-up experiments train the observable restriction in a declared 13-dimensional subspace, implement a frozen-public-encoder readout through an actual Gaussian sample channel, evaluate a fixed-coefficient sensitivity grid, and test targeted nuisance control with two-hidden-layer minibatch learning on Fashion-MNIST. The nuisance study improves shifted accuracy over ERM, while generic protected balancing accounts for most of the gain. Together, the theory and experiments identify attainable information actions, predictive costs and the separate assumptions required for population-risk certification.

papers.title: Quantum theory of a three-photon Kerr parametric oscillator: from exact solution to the Kerr-cat qutrit
papers.abstract: We investigate the quantum properties of a nonlinear Kerr oscillator driven by a three-photon pump. We identify an exact spectral degeneracy at which the interacting ground state admits a nonperturbative analytical solution. In the large-amplitude regime, the resulting manifold becomes threefold quasi-degenerate and forms delocalized three-headed quantum superpositions. Away from the exact degeneracy, we derive an approximate description of the threefold quasi-degenerate manifold in terms of $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric superpositions of squeezed coherent states. These states differ qualitatively from conventional three-component cat states due to the presence of squeezing with a distinctive parametric dependence. By varying the pump-oscillator detuning, the squeezing can be enhanced, suppressed, or even reversed, leading to a squeezing-to-anti-squeezing transition. In the large-amplitude regime, the threefold manifold defines a noise-biased bosonic qutrit, which we term a Kerr-cat qutrit. We show that photon loss predominantly induces cyclic shift errors, while clock errors are suppressed, and quantitatively characterize the resulting noise bias. We further show that the detuning controls the noise bias through the squeezing. Going beyond stabilization, we construct arbitrary operations on a single Kerr-cat qutrit together with an entangling two-qutrit gate, providing a complete set of logical operations for universal qutrit quantum computation, and validate their action through full Lindblad simulations. Our results establish the three-photon Kerr oscillator both as a rich nonlinear quantum system with analytically tractable macroscopic states and as a platform for noise-biased bosonic qutrit quantum computation.

papers.title: Hyrax: An Extensible Framework for Rapid ML Experimentation and Unsupervised Discovery in the Era of Rubin, Roman, and Euclid
papers.abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Roman Space Telescope, Euclid, and other next-generation surveys will deliver imaging, spectroscopic, and time-domain data at scales that increasingly shift the bottleneck in astronomical machine learning (ML) projects from model design to infrastructure. We present Hyrax, an open-source, modular, GPU-enabled Python framework that supports the full ML lifecycle in astronomy: from data acquisition and training to inference and experiment comparison, with capabilities including multimodal dataset support, integrated vector databases for similarity search, and interactive two- and three-dimensional latent-space exploration for unsupervised discovery. We demonstrate Hyrax's versatility through five representative applications on real survey data: (i) unsupervised representation learning on $\sim 4\times10^5$ Rubin Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) Data Preview 1 (DP1) galaxies, surfacing new merger and low-surface-brightness candidates missing from reference Euclid and Dark Energy Survey catalogs, while also isolating imaging artifacts -- all without labeled training data; (ii) hybrid density-based clustering for identifying cluster-scale gravitational lens candidates in DP1 data; (iii) multimodal early-time transient classification in the Zwicky Transient Facility leveraging light curves, spectra, images, and metadata; (iv) supervised false-positive filtering in shift-and-stack searches for distant solar system objects in the Dark Energy Camera Ecliptic Exploration Project survey; and (v) supervised detection of semi-resolved dwarf galaxies in Hyper Suprime-Cam and LSST-like imaging using synthetic source injection. Together, these results demonstrate that Hyrax provides astronomy-specific ML infrastructure that enables systematic discovery and rapid methodological iteration across next-generation astronomical surveys.

papers.title: GRASP: Graph Agentic Search over Propositions for Multi-hop Question Answering
papers.abstract: Agentic retrieval improves multi-hop question answering by giving language models autonomy to iteratively gather evidence. Recent work augments these systems with knowledge graphs for structured traversal, but this combination introduces significant cost: expensive graph construction at index time and compounding token usage at inference time. We introduce Graph Agentic Search over Propositions (GRASP), an agentic system that simultaneously optimizes for high accuracy and minimal token usage in multi-hop question answering. Rather than executing a rigid, singular query, GRASP actively coordinates its retrieval strategy by decomposing multi-hop queries into dependency-aware plans. This enables GRASP to dynamically scale the number of sub-agents according to the complexity of the problem. Each sub-agent resolves its single-hop query by exploring a novel three-layer hierarchical graph of entities, propositions, and passages, using the entity layer for targeted traversal and the proposition layer for high-recall passage retrieval via reciprocal-rank voting. We evaluate GRASP on MuSiQue, 2WikiMultihopQA, and HotpotQA under two settings: open-corpus retrieval and extended context reasoning (LongBench). GRASP achieves the highest QA accuracy in the open retrieval setting on MuSiQue and 2Wiki while using 40-50 percent fewer tokens than IRCoT+HippoRAG2. Furthermore, GRASP leads on EM and F1 across all three datasets in the LongBench setting while using 30 percent fewer tokens than the next most accurate method. Finally, we introduce success economy - the amortized token cost per correct answer, weighted by difficulty - and advocate for efficiency-aware evaluation as a standard practice for agentic QA.

papers.title: ArtMesh: Part-Aware Articulated Mesh Fields with Motion-Consistent Dynamics
papers.abstract: We present ArtMesh, a mesh-native method for reconstructing articulated objects explicitly as connected triangle meshes with per-part rigid motion from multi-view observations in start and end states. Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines for articulated reconstruction inherit the unstructured point-based geometry of their splatting base, which provides no surface topology for reasoning about part boundaries or enforcing motion consistency along the object's connectivity. ArtMesh instead builds on a mesh-based differentiable rendering backbone, enabling part-aware dynamics to act directly on the structured topology. To make the topology compatible with articulation, we introduce part-aware restricted Delaunay remeshing, producing connected submeshes whose triangles do not cross semantic part boundaries. The dynamic mesh field then optimizes articulation using bidirectional Vertex-wise Motion Consistency on transported mesh vertices and Pixel-wise Motion Consistency on rendered images. We introduce Articulate-100, a new benchmark of 100 articulated objects spanning 16 PartNet-Mobility categories. On this benchmark, given ground-truth part masks, ArtMesh achieves the best aggregate joint-axis estimation and part-level geometric reconstruction among prior 3DGS-based pipelines, with the largest gains on objects with many movable parts.

papers.title: Rotational energy levels in the ground vibrational state of methane with kHz-level accuracy from comb-referenced double-resonance and Lamb-dip spectroscopies
papers.abstract: Methane is a key spherical-top molecule, yet restrictive selection rules for one-photon transitions have prevented determination of its ground state (GS) energies with state-of-the-art kHz-level accuracy. We report the GS rotational energy level differences with kHz-level accuracy from two frequency-comb-referenced Doppler-free methods: optical-optical double-resonance spectroscopy in the $Λ$-type configuration, and Lamb-dip spectroscopy of allowed and forbidden transitions. A Hamiltonian fit to the data yields GS term values with rotational numbers up to $\it{J}$ = 12 with kHz level accuracy.

papers.title: Coreset-Induced Conditional Velocity Flow Matching
papers.abstract: We propose Coreset-Induced Conditional Velocity Flow Matching (CCVFM), a generative model that augments hierarchical rectified flow with a data-informed source distribution. Standard flow matching regresses only the conditional mean of the velocity; hierarchical flow matching instead models the full conditional velocity law with a second, inner flow in velocity space, but this inner flow is asked to transport isotropic Gaussian noise to a multimodal target velocity distribution from scratch. Our key observation is that this inner source can be replaced by a closed-form surrogate built from a coreset of the target. CCVFM first compresses the target into weighted atoms using an entropic Sinkhorn coreset and lifts them to a Gaussian mixture. The induced conditional velocity law is then a closed-form Gaussian mixture that can be sampled without a learned neural sampler. A lightweight correction flow, trained from this surrogate source, then refines the remaining surrogate-to-target residual rather than learning an entire noise-to-data map. We prove that the surrogate transport cost equals the target-surrogate Wasserstein gap under an explicit compression assumption, whereas the noise-source analogue has a dimension-scale lower bound. We further characterize the conditional second moment of the training target when the source velocity is drawn from the surrogate law independently of the target velocity, and show that the part of it that depends on the source is small when the surrogate conditional law is close to the true conditional velocity law in mean and covariance. Empirically, on MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet-32, and CelebA-HQ, the proposed method reaches competitive few-step generation under matched architectures. Code is available at https://github.com/ziwaa-se/CCVFM.

papers.title: Quantum rotation sensing from superintegrability
papers.abstract: Detection based on quantum principles such as entanglement has the capacity to achieve finessed levels of sensitivity, bringing transformative impacts to applications. In this study, we propose a rotation sensing protocol using an extended Bose-Hubbard model in a four-site configuration. The design, based on a simple population imbalance measurement to quantify rotation, profits from the property of superintegrability. The implementation of the sensing protocol achieves rotation-detection sensitivity scaling as $N^{-3/2}$, where $N$ is the number of particles. Remarkably, the sensitivity lies close to the quantum Cramér - Rao bound. Our results illustrate superintegrability opportunities for advancing the field of quantum sensing.

papers.title: 3DSS: 3D Surface Splatting for Inverse Rendering
papers.abstract: We present 3D Surface Splatting (3DSS), the first differentiable surface splatting renderer for physically-based inverse rendering from multi-view images. Our central insight is that surface separation, which groups the surfels covering a pixel by the surface they sample, can be formulated with the reconstruction kernels themselves: two surfels sample the same surface when their kernels overlap in depth. Compositing each resulting surface layer with a coverage opacity derived from its accumulated Elliptical Weighted Average (EWA) weight yields anti-aliased silhouettes and informative visibility gradients at sparsely covered edges. With forward microfacet shading under co-optimized HDR environment lighting, 3DSS jointly recovers shape, spatially-varying BRDF, and illumination, and its oriented surfels convert directly into meshes by oriented-point surface reconstruction. On the real-world Stanford-ORB and the TensoIR Synthetic benchmarks, 3DSS outperforms state-of-the-art mesh-based and major comparable implicit and Gaussian-based methods in novel view synthesis and relighting, with geometry on par with the strongest baselines.

papers.title: Time-Dependent Classical and Quantum Integrability in Sigma Models: From the $λ$-Model to the Perturbed $SU(2)_1$ WZW Model
papers.abstract: Using the Hamiltonian formulation of the $λ$-model with time-dependent coupling, we compare classical Lax and quantum integrability in the isotropic current-current deformation of the $SU(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model. From the classical WZW current algebra at fixed level, we derive equations of motion for the coupled left- and right-moving currents and construct a generalized Lax connection whose flatness fixes the integrable time-dependent coupling. Equal-time Lax-matrix Poisson brackets take the generalized Maillet form, and the $r/s$ kernels satisfy the extended classical Yang-Baxter relation. A coupling redefinition and time reparametrization relate it to the $λ$-model with local couplings. At level one, non-Abelian bosonization identifies the deformed model with the interacting isospin sector of the chiral-invariant $SU(2)$ Gross-Neveu model. In its exact generalized Bethe ansatz (GBA) solution, the quantum Yang-Baxter equation constrains the time-dependent coupling. In the universal weak-coupling regime, it shares the leading inverse-affine time dependence imposed by classical Lax flatness of the $λ$-model. This common weak-coupling equation coincides with the one-loop renormalization-group equation of the static model, with time identified with the logarithm of the UV cutoff. Periodic boundary conditions in the GBA yield the quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, whose solution gives an exact many-body wavefunction admitting a Yang-Yang representation at any nonzero drive rate. In the slow-drive limit, dynamical dimensional transmutation generates an isospin mass gap decaying exponentially in time on the decreasing-coupling branch, while in the fast-drive limit the isospin sector approaches the $SU(2)_1$ WZW UV fixed point. We also compare classical and quantum integrability of higher-level WZW and noncompact-group sigma models.

papers.title: Sharp regularity for degenerate fully nonlinear equations with oblique boundary conditions and Hamiltonian terms
papers.abstract: We prove optimal boundary $C^{1,α}$ regularity for viscosity solutions of degenerate fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations with oblique boundary conditions and Hamiltonian terms of the form \[ \begin{cases} |Du|^γF(D^2 u) + \varrho(x)|Du|^σ = f(x) & \text{in } Ω,\\ β(x)\cdot Du+ζ(x)u = g(x) & \text{on } \partial Ω, \end{cases} \] where $γ>0$ and $0<σ\le 1+γ$. We develop a compactness framework for affine translations, linking the size of the translation to the Hamiltonian structure. This is combined with a boundary improvement-of-flatness argument adapted to oblique boundary data, yielding the optimal boundary regularity.

papers.title: Job-Scheduling Games with Time-Dependent Processing Times
papers.abstract: Job-scheduling games have traditionally assumed fixed processing times. However, in many realistic environments, ranging from cyber-security response to high-frequency trading, a task's duration depends on its starting time. We study job-scheduling games with time-dependent processing times, where job lengths are linear functions of their start times, exhibiting either positive deterioration (increasing length) or negative deterioration (decreasing length). We analyze these games under various coordination mechanisms and priority policies. By introducing the concept of delay-averse agents, we provide a unifying framework to characterize equilibrium existence. For delay-averse jobs, we show that stability is maintained and pure Nash equilibria (NE) can be computed efficiently. In contrast, for non-delay-averse jobs, we demonstrate that a NE may not exist, and prove that deciding its existence is NP-complete, even on identical machines - a fundamental departure from classical coordination mechanisms. Regarding equilibrium inefficiency, we show that the Price of Anarchy (PoA) can be significantly higher than in environments with fixed processing times. To mitigate this, we propose and analyze three coordination mechanisms: SBPT (Shortest Basic Processing Time), which reduces the PoA in games with positive deterioration to a constant, and SDR (Smallest Deterioration Rate) and LBDR (Largest Basic-Deterioration Ratio) for negative deterioration, which achieve tight constant PoA bounds of $2$ and $\max\{\frac{e}{e-1}, 2-\frac{1}{m}\}$, respectively. Our results bridge the gap between centralized time-dependent scheduling and decentralized game-theoretic analysis.

papers.title: Families of Eliahou semigroups linked to Farey intervals
papers.abstract: We describe new classes of numerical semigroups with a Farey interval as a crucial parameter. We compute their Eliahou number and show many cases in which it is negative, encompassing families described by Delgado, Eliahou and Fromentin, and Bras-Amorós. We show that all these semigroups satisfy Wilf's conjecture. This work is based on an experimental search that found all Eliahou-negative semigroups with conductor up to 200 (and conjecturally up to 400) thanks to a new way of representing the semigroup and pruning off unwanted branches. This proves that Wilf's conjecture holds for conductor up to 200.

papers.title: Energetics of stochastic limit-cycle oscillators: when does coupling reduce dissipation?
papers.abstract: Non-linear oscillators occur in a wide range of biological and engineered systems. In noisy environments, the steady-state entropy production rate (EPR) quantifies time irreversibility and, under a thermodynamic interpretation, the associated energy dissipation. We study an idealized, analytically tractable family of stochastic circular limit-cycle oscillators and examine how mutual coupling in pairs and populations alters dissipation. The dynamics are characterized by a dimensionless effective temperature given by the ratio of radial relaxation and diffusion timescales. For identical oscillators, we derive analytical results for the EPR under radial, phase (Kuramoto-like), and Cartesian couplings. The phase-coupling analysis also considers nonidentical intrinsic frequencies. Coupling can increase or decrease EPR through changes in the radial mean and variance and in probability currents, with the response depending on effective temperature and system size. In particular, weak attractive Cartesian coupling lowers the EPR of identical oscillators at any effective temperature. At sufficiently low effective temperature, full Cartesian coupling produces a finite-coupling minimum below the uncoupled EPR throughout the oscillator family considered. Reduced EPR can also accompany improved individual and collective temporal coherence.

papers.title: Adaptive Slicing-Assisted Hyper Inference for Enhanced Small Object Detection in High-Resolution Imagery
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based object detectors have achieved remarkable success across numerous computer vision applications, yet they continue to struggle with small object detection in high-resolution aerial and satellite imagery, where dense object distributions, variable shooting angles, diminutive target sizes, and substantial inter-class variability pose formidable challenges. Existing slicing strategies that partition high-resolution images into manageable patches have demonstrated promising results for enlarging the effective receptive field of small targets; however, their reliance on fixed slice dimensions introduces significant redundant computation, inflating inference cost and undermining detection speed. In this paper, we propose \textbf{Adaptive Slicing-Assisted Hyper Inference (ASAHI)}, a novel slicing framework that shifts the paradigm from prescribing a fixed slice size to adaptively determining the optimal number of slices according to image resolution, thereby substantially mitigating redundant computation while preserving beneficial overlap between adjacent patches. ASAHI integrates three synergistic components: (1)an adaptive resolution-aware slicing algorithm that dynamically generates 6 or 12 overlapping patches based on a learned threshold, (2)a slicing-assisted fine-tuning (SAF) strategy that constructs augmented training data comprising both full-resolution and sliced image patches, and (3)a Cluster-DIoU-NMS (CDN) post-processing module that combines the geometric merging efficiency of Cluster-NMS with the center-distance-aware suppression of DIoU-NMS to achieve robust duplicate elimination in crowded scenes. Extensive experiments on VisDrone2019 and xView, demonstrate that ASAHI achieves state-of-the-art performance with 56.8% on VisDrone2019-DET-val and 22.7% on xView-test, while reducing inference time by 20-25% compared to the baseline SAHI method.

papers.title: An Implicit Compact-Kernel Material Point Method for Computational Solid Mechanics
papers.abstract: The numerical performance of the material point method (MPM) is strongly governed by the particle-grid kernel, which controls the trade-off among smoothness, locality, numerical diffusion, contact accuracy, and computational cost. Although wide-support smooth kernels can effectively suppress cell-crossing instability, they often introduce increased numerical diffusion, artificial contact gaps, and higher transfer cost. In contrast, the suitability of compact-kernel designs for implicit computational solid mechanics remains unclear. In this work, we develop an implicit formulation of the Compact-Kernel Material Point Method (CK-MPM) building on the framework of Liu et al. [2025], and assess its performance through benchmark problems in linear and nonlinear solid mechanics. Numerical assessment comprises cantilever bending, Hertzian contact, narrow-clearance free fall, and colliding hyperelastic rings, supplemented by a transfer-only diffusion test and spatial and temporal refinement studies. Implicit CK-MPM mitigates the cell-crossing stress noise and numerical energy loss observed in linear MPM, while retaining bending and energy responses comparable to those of quadratic B-spline MPM. Meanwhile, its more localized transfers improve contact-pressure accuracy and reduce the artificial contact gaps and early-contact artifacts associated with the wider-support quadratic kernel. These results demonstrate that the developed implicit formulation retains CK-MPM's favorable balance between smoothness and transfer locality in static and dynamic solid-mechanics analysis.

papers.title: Birational $\mathbb P^2$-bundle structures and toric 2-Fano manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a general birational program toward the classification of toric 2-Fano manifolds through the investigation of the minimal projective bundle dimension \(m(X) \in \{1,\dots,\dim(X)\}\) introduced in our previous work. This invariant captures the minimal degree of a dominating family of rational curves on \(X\) and admits a natural combinatorial interpretation in terms of centered primitive collections. We establish a general obstruction to being 2-Fano in terms of the existence of projective bundle structures and prove a birational reduction theorem for toric Fano manifolds with \(m(X)=2\). This allows us to show that the only toric 2-Fano manifold \(X\) with \(m(X) = 2\) is \(X\cong \mathbb{P}^2\). We also investigate how this strategy might extend to \(m\ge3\).

papers.title: The Quantum Kicked Rotor: A Paradigm of Quantum Chaos. Foundational aspects and new perspectives
papers.abstract: The kicked rotor provides a simple yet powerful model for introducing many of the central concepts of classical and quantum chaos. Despite its apparent simplicity, it exhibits rich dynamical behavior and has found applications across a wide range of fields, including atomic and optical physics, condensed matter physics, and emerging quantum technologies. This chapter begins by exploring foundational ideas using the kicked rotor as a unifying framework. We first discuss the transition from regular to chaotic motion in the classical system, and then introduce key quantum phenomena such as dynamical localization and quantum resonances. Special attention is devoted to the emergence of characteristic time scales and their role in the quantum-classical correspondence. To make these ideas more concrete, we also provide a brief overview of experimental realizations of the kicked rotor and its variants, illustrating how theoretical concepts are implemented in practice. In the second part of the chapter, we guide the reader toward more recent and advanced developments. Topics include near-resonant dynamics, topological features of kicked systems, the emergence of quantum dynamical phases inferred from classical transport properties, and extensions to non-Hermitian physics. We conclude with a discussion of open problems and future perspectives, outlining directions in which the kicked rotor continues to offer valuable insights.

papers.title: Patterns in Individual Blood Count Trajectories in the UK Biobank Characterise Disease-Specific Signatures and May Anticipate Pan-Cancer Risk
papers.abstract: Routine blood tests are typically interpreted as individual measurements against population-derived reference ranges, with limited use of information contained in changes across repeated tests. Here, we investigate whether trends in routinely measured haematological markers can reveal patterns associated with ageing and disease progression across cancers, cardiovascular diseases and infections. Using retrospective Complete Blood Count (CBC) data from the UK Biobank, we examine changes in individual biomarkers and their relationships across successive measurements, while assessing potential confounding factors. We combine statistical analysis, machine learning and network-based approaches to identify patterns associated with different disease states and stages. We find that clinically relevant information is contained not only in absolute blood-cell counts, but also in the direction, magnitude and coordinated patterns of change between measurements. These patterns provide candidate disease signatures that may complement conventional interpretation based on individual values and reference intervals. Because the approach relies on inexpensive tests already collected routinely in clinical practice, it offers a practical route for extracting additional clinical information from existing data, with potential applications in earlier disease detection, monitoring and precision healthcare.

papers.title: Combining the Mass--Radius Posteriors of PSR J0030+0451 Allowing for Unknown Correlations and Model Systematics
papers.abstract: The NASA Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer (\emph{NICER}) mission measures the X-ray pulse profiles of millisecond pulsars and uses pulse profile modeling (PPM) techniques to constrain their masses ($M$) and radii ($R$), in order to probe the state of matter in their interiors. One of the most studied pulsars, PSR J0030+0451, has been analyzed by multiple groups using different choices of hotspot models. The different choices of hotspot prescriptions to fit the same observational data led to different $M$--$R$ posteriors that do not completely agree with one another, resulting in a practical bottleneck for dense-matter equation-of-state (EoS) inference. In this paper, we adapt a Bayesian combination framework to the published $M$--$R$ posteriors of PSR J0030+0451 while allowing for unknown correlations and systematic uncertainties. Using this technique, we combine eight existing $M$--$R$ posteriors into a single estimate of the source parameters. The resulting constraint is $M=1.53^{+0.31}_{-0.27}\,M_\odot$, $R=13.44^{+2.95}_{-2.38}\,\mathrm{km}$, and compactness $C=0.169^{+0.018}_{-0.021}$ (68\% credible intervals). The combined distribution retains the lower- and higher-mass solutions obtained with different hotspot models. Conditional interpolation with PSR~J0437--4715 gives $R_{1.4}=11.84^{+0.88}_{-0.83}\,\mathrm{km}$. Our results provide a combined $M$--$R$ constraint for J0030+0451 that accounts for shared observations and cross-model uncertainty, and a framework for combining correlated measurements of the same source.

papers.title: Musculoskeletal Motion Imitation for Learning Joint-Agnostic Exoskeleton Controllers in Healthy and Impaired Gait
papers.abstract: Designing generalizable control policies for lower-limb exoskeletons is often constrained by the need for large biomechanics datasets or lengthy human-in-the-loop optimization. To address this challenge, we introduce a joint-agnostic framework that combines physiologically plausible musculoskeletal simulation with reinforcement learning to enable scalable exoskeleton assistance for both healthy individuals and those with muscle weakness. Our base control policy reproduces both the kinematics and kinetics of healthy reference gait. Fine-tuned from the base policy, the resulting exoskeleton control policies produce assistive torque profiles at the hip, knee, and ankle that align with those validated in human experiments. For simulated impaired-gait models, the learned control policies yield asymmetric, deficit-specific exoskeleton assistance that improves both metabolic cost and bilateral kinematic symmetry without explicit prescription of the assistance pattern. We further deployed the learned controller on a robotic hip exoskeleton, where the applied torque closely matched the simulated teacher and reduced the net metabolic rate by 6.9% in three healthy participants. These results indicate that musculoskeletal motion imitation can potentially serve as a scalable foundation for exoskeleton control across joints and across healthy gait and gait affected by lower-limb muscle weakness, reducing the need for extensive physical trials. The project page is available at https://ichoi02.github.io/Imitation-Exo/.

papers.title: BLADE: Better Language Answers through Dialogue and Explanations
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based educational assistants often provide direct answers offering little incentive for students to explore or engage with course materials. We present BLADE (Better Language Answers through Dialogue and Explanations), a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) based conversational assistant grounded in course-specific content that guides students toward relevant materials through citation-grounded dialogue rather than delivering unsourced solutions. We evaluate BLADE in an advanced undergraduate NLP course with extensive instructional resources, in which locating and synthesizing relevant material is a central challenge. During quizzes, students are assigned to one of three conditions: BLADE only, direct course materials only, or both; we measure performance and resource usage. Results show that students consistently select BLADE over direct materials when both are available, and that quiz performance is highest when students use BLADE alone. In contrast, simultaneous use of both resources is associated with significantly lower performance. No statistically significant difference in quiz performance occurred between assigned resource conditions. These findings show the potential of RAG-based assistants as a citation-grounded interface for applying course content under open-book exam-like conditions, while suggesting that adding direct-material access does not necessarily improve in-task performance.

papers.title: A High-Order Fast Direct Solver for Surface PDEs on Triangles
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a triangular formulation of the hierarchical Poincaré--Steklov (HPS) method for elliptic partial differential equations on surfaces. It admits high-order discretizations on unstructured triangular meshes of complex geometries, with spectral collocation in the orthogonal Dubiner basis on each element. As in quadrilateral HPS, local solution operators and Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps are built and merged hierarchically, yielding a fast direct solver with $\mathcal O(N \log N)$ complexity for repeated solves on meshes with $N$ elements. Since the precomputed operators are reused for every elliptic solve, the solver also accelerates high-order implicit time-stepping schemes on surfaces. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order convergence under mesh refinement and spectral accuracy under polynomial refinement for static and time-dependent test problems.

papers.title: Sensitivity of Electromagnetic Moments to Nuclear Forces
papers.abstract: Nuclear electromagnetic moments can be precisely measured across the nuclear chart, yet understanding how they emerge from the underlying nuclear force is an open challenge for nuclear theory. Using a global emulator of ab initio calculations, we show that, unlike binding energies and charge radii, magnetic and quadrupole moments probe components of the chiral interaction that vary strongly with neutron number. We demonstrate this sensitivity with the properties of calcium isotopes, where measured moments reveal information that is largely hidden from bulk observables. We then demonstrate a method to address the inverse problem, using selected experimental magnetic moments to constrain and reorganize the allowed parameter space of the nuclear force, improving predictions beyond the calibration set while preserving descriptions of other nuclear properties.

papers.title: Consumer Search and Social Learning in Agentic Markets
papers.abstract: Motivated by agentic markets -- where AI tools facilitate search -- we propose a model of consumer search and market-wide learning. A sequence of consumers engage in costly search to acquire progressively refined signals of product fit prior to purchase. The market observes acquired signals and post-transaction feedback thereby impacting future searches. We solve for the per-consumer optimal search policy and characterize the steady-state of the learning dynamics. Search technologies (agentic or otherwise) that reduce costs at fixed inspection depth improve long-run learning and consumer surplus. In a special case with screen-level feedback, more informative search also improves these outcomes. In contrast, we show through counterexamples and numerical simulations that more informative search can degrade long-run learning and consumer surplus when the market observes only aggregate inspection and transaction feedback, highlighting the importance of feedback design.

papers.title: Parallelizable Feynman-Kac Models for Universal Probabilistic Programming
papers.abstract: We study provably correct and efficient instantiations of Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) inference in the context of formal operational semantics of Probabilistic Programs (PPs). We focus on universal PPs featuring sampling from arbitrary measures and conditioning/reweighting in unbounded loops. We first equip Probabilistic Program Graphs (PPGs), an automata-theoretic description format of PPs, with an expectation-based semantics over infinite execution traces, which also incorporates trace weights. We then prove a finite approximation theorem that provides bounds to this semantics based on expectations taken over finite, fixed-length traces. This enables us to frame our semantics within a Feynman-Kac (FK) model, and ensures the consistency of the Particle Filtering (PF) algorithm, an instance of SMC, with respect to our semantics. Building on these results, we introduce VPF, a vectorized version of the PF algorithm tailored to PPGs and our semantics. Experiments conducted with a proof-of-concept implementation of VPF show very promising results compared to state-of-the-art PP inference tools.

papers.title: A Framework for Closed-Loop Robotic Assembly, Alignment and Self-Recovery of Precision Optical Systems
papers.abstract: Robotic automation has transformed scientific workflows in domains such as chemistry and materials science, yet free-space optics, which is a high-precision domain, remains largely manual. Optical systems impose strict spatial and angular tolerances, and their performance is governed by tightly coupled physical parameters, making generalizable automation particularly challenging. In this work, we present a robotics framework for the autonomous construction, alignment, and maintenance of precision optical systems. Our approach integrates a hierarchical computer vision system, optimization routines, and custom-built tools to achieve this functionality. As a representative demonstration, we perform the fully autonomous construction of a tabletop laser cavity from randomly distributed components. The system performs several tasks such as laser beam centering, spatial alignment of multiple beams, resonator alignment, laser mode selection, and self-recovery from induced misalignment and disturbances. By achieving closed-loop autonomy for highly sensitive optical systems, this work establishes a foundation for autonomous optical experiments for applications across scientific domains.

papers.title: Lossless propagation of gain-compensated graphene plasmons
papers.abstract: Graphene plasmons offer strong electromagnetic confinement and electrical tunability, but dissipation in the graphene sheet limits their propagation. Here, we investigate how optical gain in the surrounding dielectrics can compensate these losses in single- and double-layer graphene. Starting from the full electromagnetic boundary conditions and a finite-temperature graphene conductivity, we derive the compensation condition for a single sheet and the separate optical and acoustic dispersion relations for two coupled sheets. We show that the required gain depends both on material loss and on where the gain is placed. When gain is present throughout the dielectric environment, the two double-layer modes have nearly identical compensation thresholds. When it is confined to the spacer or the outer claddings, their thresholds separate because the modes overlap differently with each region. Full-wave finite-element simulations reproduce the predicted branches and field symmetries and show a strong suppression of attenuation together with a substantial increase in propagation length. The analysis also identifies the range over which a local conductivity provides a controlled description. These results show how the spatial distribution of gain can be used to control the compensation thresholds of the optical and acoustic graphene plasmons.

papers.title: Architecture-Agnostic Feature Synergy for Universal Defense Against Heterogeneous Generative Threats
papers.abstract: Generative AI deployment poses unprecedented challenges to content safety and privacy. However, existing defense mechanisms are often tailored to specific architectures (e.g., Diffusion Models or GANs), creating fragile "defense silos" that fail against heterogeneous generative threats. This paper identifies a fundamental optimization barrier in naive pixel-space ensemble strategies: due to divergent objective functions, pixel-level gradients from heterogeneous generators become statistically orthogonal, causing destructive interference. To overcome this, we observe that despite disparate low-level mechanisms, high-level feature representations of generated content exhibit alignment across architectures. Based on this, we propose the Architecture-Agnostic Targeted Feature Synergy (ATFS) framework. By introducing a target guidance image, ATFS reformulates multi-model defense as a unified feature space alignment task, enabling intrinsic gradient alignment without complex rectification. Extensive experiments show ATFS achieves SOTA protection in heterogeneous scenarios (e.g., Diffusion+GAN). It converges rapidly, reaching over 90% performance within 40 iterations, and maintains strong attack potency even under tight perturbation budgets. The framework seamlessly extends to unseen architectures (e.g., VQ-VAE) by switching the feature extractor, and demonstrates robust resistance to JPEG compression and scaling. Being computationally efficient and lightweight, ATFS offers a viable pathway to dismantle defense silos and enable universal generative security. Code and models are open-sourced for reproducibility.

papers.title: First-Class Relationships as a Representation Threshold: Identity, Time, Confidence, and Causation
papers.abstract: Operational records -- who may access what, what changed, what caused an incident -- consist of relationships that involve several parties, hold for a period, are believed with some confidence, and cause one another. We ask what a representation must provide to store such records directly. We state four storage requirements: n-ary relationships with attributes, temporal validity, confidence with an evidential basis, and causal links between relationships. Under our definitions, each requires relationships to have identity: every relationship is stored, fetched and queried as an object with its own key. Confidence with an evidential basis and causal links also require composition: any relationship can take part in another. With n-ary relationships, either one therefore requires first-class relationships, which are identified, carry attributes, and compose at every arity. Conversely, first-class relationships suffice for all four. They are thus a threshold, and it belongs to the relationship construct, not to the data model around it: where a model's own construct falls short, every representation meeting n-ary relationships together with evidence-backed confidence or causal links builds a first-class construct from other parts, as our SQL implementation does. We place SQL, property graphs, RDF 1.2 and TypeDB relative to the threshold, and present the Attributed Temporal Causal Hypergraph (ATCH), which meets all four requirements with query operators for each.

papers.title: Stable Mechanisms
papers.abstract: We study mechanism design environments in which the designer does not know the distribution of agents' private information and draws inferences from the behavior induced by the mechanism itself. A mechanism is stable if it is optimal under some belief consistent with the information it generates, and robustly stable if this property survives small informational perturbations. We establish a fictitious revelation principle: any incentive-compatible mechanism admits a representation as a direct mechanism paired with an information filter, preserving both outcomes and informational content. Applying the framework to the classic monopoly problem, we show that, under regularity of the true type distribution, robustly stable mechanisms coincide with optimal mechanisms under that distribution, as if it were known to the designer. In general, however, posted-price mechanisms can remain robustly stable at local revenue maxima, so globally suboptimal prices can persist.

papers.title: Data Unfolding: From Problem Formulation to Result Assessment
papers.abstract: Experimental data in particle and nuclear physics, particle astrophysics, and radiation protection dosimetry are collected using experimental facilities that consist of a complex system of sensors, electronics, and software. Measured spectra or cross sections are considered as Probability Density Functions (PDFs) that deviate from true PDFs due to resolution, bias, and efficiency effects. Unfolding is viewed as a procedure for estimating an unknown true PDF. Reliable estimates of the true PDF are necessary for testing theoretical models, comparing results from different experiments, and combining results from various research endeavors. Both external and internal quality assessment methods can be applied for this purpose. In some cases, external criteria exist to evaluate deconvolution quality. A typical example is the deconvolution of a blurred image, where the sharpness of the restored image serves as an indicator of quality. However, defining such external criteria can be challenging, particularly when a measurement has not been performed previously. This paper discusses various internal criteria for assessing the quality of the results independently of external information, as well as factors that influence the quality of the unfolded distribution.

papers.title: Engineered Simultaneity: The Physical Impossibility of Consolidated Price Discovery Across Spacelike-Separated Exchanges
papers.abstract: We define engineered simultaneity: the construction of a system that requires temporal comparison of events at spacelike-separated locations, implements this comparison via an implicit simultaneity convention, and represents the result as an objective measurement rather than a conventional choice. We show that the National Best Bid and Offer (NBBO) -- the cornerstone of U.S. equity markets -- is an instance of engineered simultaneity. The NBBO requires determining "current" prices across exchanges whose spatial separation places their price events outside each other's light cones. Special relativity proves that the temporal ordering of such events is frame-dependent: there exist inertial reference frames in which the NBBO differs from the value reported by the Securities Information Processor. The impossibility is not approximate; it is exact and unavoidable within the causal structure of Minkowski spacetime, and general relativity and indefinite causal order only compound it. We formalize the argument using the causal precedence relation and connect it to Lamport's theorem on distributed ordering. The operational form of the result needs no moving observers: the NBBO depends on where it is computed, and every participant who is not at the consolidation point holds a different one. The same construction recurs inside a single exchange, where orders are stamped at a perimeter and sorted by the stamp. Read as a practitioner suggests, as a bound on the worst-case error of distributed price discovery, the NBBO is defensible, and we propose that it be published as one. We separate what a central market is for (aggregating supply and demand) from what the latency race is about (sequencing arrivals), note that races of this kind cost about $5 billion a year in global equities, and record that in June 2026 the SEC proposed to rescind the order protection rule that makes the NBBO binding.

papers.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Cognitive Complexity in LLMs via Linear Probing using Bloom's Taxonomy
papers.abstract: The black-box nature of Large Language Models necessitates novel evaluation frameworks that transcend surface-level performance metrics. This study investigates the internal neural representations of the levels of complexity using Bloom's Taxonomy as a hierarchical lens. By analyzing high-dimensional activation vectors from different LLMs, we probe whether different Bloom levels, ranging from basic recall (Remember) to abstract synthesis (Create), are linearly separable within the model's residual streams. Our results demonstrate that linear classifiers achieve high accuracy across all Bloom levels, providing evidence that level information is encoded in a linearly accessible subspace of the model's representations. These findings provide evidence that the model organizes representations according to Bloom categories early in the forward pass, with representations becoming increasingly separable across layers.

papers.title: Coulomb Interaction and Density-Independent Exciton-Scattering Processes in Atomically Thin Semiconductors
papers.abstract: In quantum-kinetic approaches to the dynamics of Coulomb-bound many-body correlations such as excitons, trions, biexcitons or higher-order correlations, a detailed knowledge of the many-body Coulomb Hamiltonian serving as a starting point is important. In this manuscript, the second-quantized description of the Coulomb interaction between Bloch electrons in a Heisenberg-equation-of-motion approach in atomically thin semiconductors is derived and reviewed. Emphasis is put on a discussion of Umklapp processes and the dielectric screening including all local-field effects. A link between \textit{ab initio} methods of screening and few-band models in effective-mass approximations for the quantum kinetics is established and important Coulomb scattering processes contributing to the exciton energy landscape and density-independent exciton scattering are discussed.

papers.title: Channel Uncertainty-Aware Robust Beamforming for RIS-Assisted RSMA Communication With Movable Antennas
papers.abstract: This work investigates a robust resource allocation framework for a downlink multi-user communication system integrating movable antennas (MAs) and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) under the rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) transmission protocol. Unlike conventional fixed-position antenna architectures, the considered MAs-enabled system introduces spatially adaptive channel variations in which antenna positions directly influence the effective channel responses. Under imperfect channel state information (CSI), changes in the MAs positions and RIS reflection coefficients affect both the estimated effective channels and the corresponding uncertainty radii under the adopted uncertainty model. This dependence leads to a highly coupled robust optimization problem. To address this challenge, we formulate a system sum-rate maximization problem by jointly optimizing the transmit precoding vectors, RIS reflection matrix, common-rate allocation, and MAs positions, subject to quality-of-service (QoS), power-budget, common-rate decoding, and minimum antenna-separation constraints. The resulting non-convex problem is efficiently handled through an iterative robust optimization framework, where the original problem is successively decomposed into active beamforming, RIS reflection matrix, and MAs position optimization subproblems, and tractable convex surrogate functions are constructed to enable iterative optimization. Moreover, conservative bounds on the common- and private-stream rates are derived under the bounded CSI uncertainty model to enforce the rate requirements within the adopted uncertainty sets. Finally, extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significant performance gains and enhanced robustness compared with benchmark schemes, while also exhibiting fast and stable convergence behavior under practical imperfect CSI conditions.

papers.title: Learned Finite Element-based Regularization of the Inverse Problem in Electrocardiographic Imaging
papers.abstract: Electrocardiographic imaging (ECGI) seeks to reconstruct cardiac electrical activity from body-surface potentials noninvasively. However, the associated inverse problem is severely ill-posed and requires robust regularization. While classical approaches primarily employ spatial smoothing, the temporal structure of cardiac dynamics remains underexploited despite its physiological relevance. We introduce a space-time regularization framework that couples spatial regularization with a learned temporal Fields-of-Experts (FoE) prior to capture complex spatiotemporal activation patterns. We derive a finite element discretization on unstructured cardiac surface meshes, prove Mosco-convergence, and develop a scalable optimization algorithm capable of handling the FoE term. Numerical experiments on synthetic epicardial data demonstrate improved denoising and inverse reconstructions compared to handcrafted spatiotemporal methods, yielding solutions that are both robust to noise and physiologically plausible.

papers.title: BayesFlow 2: Multi-Backend Amortized Bayesian Inference in Python
papers.abstract: Modern Bayesian inference involves a mixture of computational methods for estimating, validating, and drawing conclusions from probabilistic models as part of principled workflows. An overarching motif of many Bayesian methods is that they are relatively slow, which often becomes prohibitive when fitting complex models to large data sets. Amortized Bayesian inference (ABI) offers a path to solving the computational challenges of Bayes. ABI trains neural networks on model simulations, rewarding users with rapid inference of any model-implied quantity, such as point estimates, likelihoods, or full posterior distributions. In this work, we present the Python library BayesFlow, Version 2, for general-purpose ABI. Along with direct posterior, likelihood, and ratio estimation, the software includes support for multiple popular deep learning backends, a rich collection of generative networks for sampling and density estimation, complete customization and high-level interfaces, as well as new capabilities for hyperparameter optimization, design optimization, and multilevel modeling. Using a case study on dynamical system parameter estimation, combined with comparisons to similar software, we show that our streamlined, user-friendly workflow has strong potential to support broad adoption.

papers.title: Design-Conditional Prior Elicitation for Dirichlet Process Mixtures: A Unified Framework for Cluster Counts and Weight Control
papers.abstract: Dirichlet process mixtures (DPMs) model variation in effects across sites or studies and in latent traits among examinees. The concentration parameter affects both the number of clusters in the sample and the population weights, yet its hyperprior is often chosen by default. We describe a method for choosing this hyperprior when the number of units is fixed by design. We calibrate a Gamma hyperprior to the analyst's expected cluster count and uncertainty about it, then examine the implied weights. If count and weight judgments conflict, Dual-Anchor selects a compromise and reports its implications for both. Across our simulations and applications, the choice of prior could change the inferred number of clusters considerably even when individual estimates changed little. A higher cluster count under an alternative prior warrants a closer look at the upper tail, where estimates can shift even when the median remains stable. The DPprior R package implements the calibration and diagnostics.

papers.title: Ultrasensitive, universal single-ion nanodetector
papers.abstract: In this paper, a carbon nanotube (CNT) based single-ion detector is proposed and its performance is evaluated with atomistic quantum transport models. The sensor can detect any ion type without molecule-specific functionalization and allows for continuous real-time ion monitoring. A single ion temporarily changes the operating principle of the sensor's CNT field-effect transistor into a resonant tunneling diode. The concrete device example of this paper showed a source-drain current increase of 5 orders of magnitude induced by a single ion.

papers.title: Concentration Inequalities for Exchangeable Tensors and Matrix-valued Data
papers.abstract: We study concentration inequalities for structured weighted sums of random data, including (i) tensor inner products and (ii) sequential matrix sums. We are interested in tail bounds and concentration inequalities for those structured weighted sums under exchangeability, extending beyond the classical framework of independent terms. We develop Hoeffding and Bernstein bounds provided with structure-dependent exchangeability. Along the way, we recover known results in weighted sum of exchangeable random variables and i.i.d. sums of random matrices to the optimal constants. We also derive a concentration bound for combinatorial sums of matrix arrays with an improved constant in the bias term compared with that by the method of exchangeable pairs. For applications, the richer structures provide us with novel analytical tools for estimating the average effect of multi-factor response models and studying fixed-design sketching methods in federated averaging. We apply our results to these problems, and find that our theoretical predictions are corroborated by numerical evidence.

papers.title: Deep Delta Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce Deep Delta Learning (DDL), which replaces the additive residual update of the Transformer with the delta rule applied across depth. A standard sublayer adds its output to the residual stream regardless of what the stream already holds. In DDL, each attention or MLP sublayer selects a direction, reads the state along it, and writes a gated rank-1 correction proportional to the error between a learned target and that readout. A single gate interpolates between skipping the sublayer and overwriting the selected component, and every orthogonal direction stays on the identity path. The same rule extends to a residual stream with several value channels per feature, which enlarges the persistent state of the model while attention and MLP widths stay fixed. In decoder-only language models at GPT-2 small and medium scales, each pretrained on 49.15B FineWeb-Edu tokens, every DDL variant reaches lower validation loss and higher mean one-shot accuracy on eight downstream tasks than the additive baseline, with fewer than 0.3% additional parameters.

papers.title: Probing gluon saturation with forward di-hadron correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
papers.abstract: We present a detailed numerical investigation of semi-inclusive forward di-hadron production in proton--nucleus collisions employing the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. We focus on the regime where di-hadrons are produced nearly back-to-back in the transverse plane, thereby justifying a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization approach in terms of small-$x$ gluon distributions. Our computation integrates several key elements: i) non-linear rapidity evolution via the Balitsky--Kovchegov equation with running coupling, ii) both perturbative and non-perturbative Sudakov resummation, and iii) a phenomenologically constrained model for the initial conditions for small-$x$ gluon distributions. We compare this phenomenological framework to experimental data from the STAR Collaboration on azimuthal correlations in forward di-pion production in both proton--proton and proton--gold collisions. We analyze the systematic theoretical uncertainties associated with the saturation scales of nuclei at the initial scale for rapidity evolution and with those associated with the hadronization process. Finally, we make predictions for the kinematics anticipated to be covered by the ALICE Forward Calorimeter (FoCal) upgrade at the Large Hadron Collider.

papers.title: Antisymmetrization of composite fermionic states for quantum simulations of nuclear reactions in first-quantization mapping
papers.abstract: I present a first-quantization deterministic algorithm for antisymmetrizing a spatially separated target-projectile system containing $N_T$ and $N_p$ identical fermions, respectively. The method constructs a fully antisymmetric wavefunction from the product of two independently antisymmetrized many-body states, each of which may be a superposition of Slater determinants. The algorithm uses a Dicke-state ancilla register that coherently encodes all one-particle exchange channels between the two subsystems and, crucially, requires only single-particle swaps to generate the full antisymmetric structure. After consolidating distinct control conditions using logical or operations, the optimized circuit uses $N_TN_p$ single-particle exchanges, up to $N_p$ of which can be performed in parallel. The correct fermionic phase is incorporated through the application of $Z$ gates on $N_T$ ancillae, after which the ancilla register is efficiently uncomputed using a compact sequence of controlled operations. This construction provides a nontrivial and scalable protocol for preparing fully antisymmetric states in reaction and scattering simulations, significantly expanding the range of systems that can be addressed with first-quantized quantum algorithms.

papers.title: Deepfakes in the 2025 Canadian Election: Prevalence, Partisanship, and Platform Dynamics
papers.abstract: Concerns about AI-generated political content are growing, yet there is limited empirical evidence on how deepfakes appear and circulate across social platforms during major events in democratic countries. We analyze the 2025 Canadian federal election across X, Bluesky, and Reddit using a high-accuracy detector trained on diverse modern generative models, covering 187,778 posts. We find that 5.9% of election-related images were deepfakes. Right-leaning accounts shared them more often (9.2% of images flagged) than left-leaning users (3.9%), with flagged content more frequently defamatory or conspiratorial. Yet, most detected deepfakes were benign or non-political, and harmful ones drew little attention, accounting for only 0.1% of all views on X. Overall, deepfakes were present in the election conversation, but their reach was modest, and realistic fabricated images, although less common, drew higher engagement, highlighting growing concerns about their misuses.

papers.title: CoDeQ: Compression with a Dead-Zone Quantizer for Differentiable Joint Pruning--Quantization
papers.abstract: Joint pruning and quantization can reduce the inference cost of neural-networks, but determining layerwise sparsity and precision often requires auxiliary allocation procedures and considerable hyperparameter tuning. We introduce CoDeQ, a quantization-aware training method that unifies pruning and quantization through a learnable dead-zone quantizer. Its learned dead-zone width controls layerwise sparsity, while bit widths can be held fixed or learned in mixed-precision mode. A pruning-aware scale allocates all available nonzero reconstruction levels over the retained range. We derive the spacing that minimizes worst-case reconstruction error over this range for a fixed bit width and range endpoint. Model weights and compression parameters are optimized jointly under one global compression coefficient, with a shared learning rate for the compression parameters. On VGG7/CIFAR-10, CoDeQ with 2-bit activations achieves 0.05% relative BOPs, for an accuracy drop of 0.32 percentage points. On DeiT-Tiny/ImageNet-1K, mixed-precision CoDeQ preserves FP32-level accuracy at only 8.12% relative BOPs. Additional experiments across several architectures and datasets demonstrate competitive accuracy--BOP trade-offs against other joint compression methods.

papers.title: Free wreath products by finite group duals
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb G$ be a compact quantum group and let $Λ$ be a finite group. We study $\mathbb W(\mathbb G,Λ):=\mathbb G\wr_{*,β_Λ}\widehatΛ$, a natural family parallel to Bichon's free wreath products $\mathbb G\wr_*S_N^+$. We obtain an explicit formula for the Haar state of $\mathbb W(\mathbb G,Λ)$. Under natural Kac-type factoriality assumptions, we also derive central decompositions of the associated von Neumann and reduced C*-algebras, with full ${\rm II}_1$-factor and simple unique-trace summands.

papers.title: A new class of affine $K(π,1)$ arrangements
papers.abstract: We show that a certain class of affine hyperplane arrangements are $K(π,1)$ by endowing their Falk complexes with an injective metric. This gives new examples of infinite $K(π,1)$ arrangements in dimension $n>2$.

papers.title: Assemble the Puzzle: Cross-Agent Utility-Aware Feature Scheduling for Bandwidth-Limited Cooperative Perception
papers.abstract: Cooperative perception (CP) lets connected vehicles and roadside units detect objects beyond the inherent range limitation and occlusion of single-agent systems, yet its practicality is constrained by limited Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication bandwidth. Existing methods improve bandwidth efficiency by letting collaborating agents send only selected feature cells driven by local detection confidence, serving a centralized ego agent's request. They overlook realistic communication scheduling and neglect cross-agent redundancy. We present JigsawComm, a decentralized utility-aware feature scheduling framework that learns to ``assemble the puzzle'' of multi-agent features. Choosing who sends each region requires a utility that measures what each agent's features contribute to the collaboration. JigsawComm incorporates a lightweight feature utility estimator, learned without utility labels from the cooperative model's own leave-one-agent-out counterfactuals, which aligns utilities onto a single comparable scale across agents. From one broadcast of compact utility maps, every agent ranks the observers of each cell and sends the cells it observes best to maximize coverage and, budget permitting, second best for accuracy refinement. Each agent also broadcasts its onboard detector's lightweight bounding box list, enabling an intermediate-late hybrid fusion with our feature-anchored box consensus, which synergistically enhances the final perception results with all available observations. With every transmitted byte counted, JigsawComm at 0.45 KB per vehicle outperforms all baselines on the real-world V2X-Real benchmark, and under measured C-V2X traces on CooperScene it retains 74.5 of its 79.8 AP@0.5, at least 15.5 points above every prior art baseline.

papers.title: On fractional triangle decompositions of random graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that with high probability $G(n,p)$ with $p \geq n^{-4/11 + o(1)}$ admits a fractional triangle decomposition (FTD), i.e., a nonnegative weighting of its triangles such that for each edge, the total weight of the triangles containing it equals one. This improves on the state of the art, due to Delcourt, Kelly, and Postle, that $p \geq n^{-1/3+o(1)}$ suffices. The proof is algorithmic: Given $G \sim G(n,p)$, we first construct an approximate FTD by taking a uniform weighting of the triangles. We then use specialized gadgets to iteratively shift weights and obtain successively better approximations of an FTD.

papers.title: On the Sum of Element Orders in Finite Abelian Groups
papers.abstract: Let $ψ(G) = \sum_{g \in G} o(g)$ denote the sum of element orders of a finite group $G$. It is known that among groups of order $n$, the cyclic group $C_n$ maximizes $ψ$. Tărnăuceanu proved that two finite abelian $p$-groups of the same order are isomorphic if and only if they have the same sum of element orders, and conjectured this for arbitrary finite abelian groups. In this paper, we confirm the conjecture by proving a stronger result: for finite $LCM$-groups $G$ and $H$ of the same order, $ψ(G) = ψ(H)$ if and only if $G$ and $H$ have the same order type.

papers.title: Proper kernels in microlocal sheaf theory
papers.abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be real analytic manifolds and let $Λ\subseteq T^*X$ and $Σ\subseteq T^*Y$ be closed conic subanalytic singular isotropics. Given a sheaf $K \in \mathrm{Sh}_{-Λ\times Σ}(X \times Y)$ microsupported in $-Λ\times Σ$, consider the convolution functor $(-) \ast K \colon \mathrm{Sh}_Λ(X) \rightarrow \mathrm{Sh}_Σ(Y)$ from sheaves microsupported in $Λ$ to sheaves microsupported in $Σ$. We show that the convolution functor $(-) \ast K$ preserves compact objects if and only if for each $x \in X$, the restriction $K|_{\{x\} \times Y} \in \mathrm{Sh}_Σ(Y)$ is a compact object. By a result of Kuo-Li, the functor sending a sheaf kernel $K$ to the convolution functor $(-) \ast K$ is an equivalence between the category $\mathrm{Sh}_{-Λ\times Σ}(X \times Y)$ of sheaves microsupported in $-Λ\times Σ$ and the category of cocontinuous functors from $\mathrm{Sh}_Λ(X)$ to $\mathrm{Sh}_Σ(Y)$. We therefore classify all cocontinuous functors that preserve compact objects between the two categories. Our approach is entirely categorical and requires minimal input from geometry: we introduce the notion of a proper object in a compactly generated stable infinity-category and study its properties under strongly continuous localizations to obtain the result. The main geometric input is the analysis of compact and proper objects of the category of $P$-constructible sheaves for a triangulation $P$ of a manifold $Z$ via the exit path category $\mathrm{Exit}(Z, P) \simeq P$. Along the way, we show that a sheaf $F \in \mathrm{Sh}_Λ(X)$ is proper if and only if it has perfect stalks, which is equivalent to a result of Nadler.

papers.title: JWST Observations of SN 2024ggi II: NIRSpec Spectroscopy and CO Modeling at 285 and 385 Days Past the Explosion
papers.abstract: We present James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) NIRSpec observations of SN~2024ggi, spanning wavelengths of 1.7--5.5 micron at +285.51 and +385.27 days post-explosion. These nebular spectra are dominated by asymmetric emission lines from atomic species including H, Ca, Ar, C, Mg, Ni, Co, and Fe, indicative of an aspherical explosion. The other strong features are molecular CO vibrational bands from the fundamental and first overtone. We introduce a novel, data-driven approach using non-LTE 3D radiative transfer simulations to model the CO emission with high fidelity. This method enables us to constrain the three-dimensional CO distribution and its radial temperature structure. CO formation is found to occur prior to day +285, with subsequent evolution characterized by progressive evaporation. The CO mass decreases from approximately (7.9 to 1.0)e-4 Msol, while the average temperature drops from about 2300 K to 1800 K. Concurrently, the CO distribution becomes increasingly clumped (f_c = 5.5 to 10). The minimum velocity of the CO-emitting region decreases (v1=1400 to 800 km/s), above the receding photosphere velocity (vph=500 km/s), suggesting the photosphere resides within Si-rich layers. However, the temperature profile indicates that only a narrow zone reaches the conditions necessary for SiO formation. Due to a lack of observational constraints, SiO clumping is not modeled, and thus, synthetic SiO profiles for mass estimates are not highlighted. We discuss the implications of these findings for dust formation processes in SN2024ggi.

papers.title: Analysis of Variational Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Variational sparse autoencoders (vSAEs) replace a sparse autoencoder's deterministic Top-K mechanism with a sampled Gaussian posterior hypothesized to produce a more robust feature dictionary. To test this, we build permutation comparisons over training seeds for custom analyses, and score two popular benchmarks on one pair of existing checkpoints. When fixing the unit variance and ablating sampling on the vSAE, we find that the gap between the non-sampled vSAE and a Top-K SAE with an L2 activation penalty can be decomposed completely into a set of five implementation details. When we enable sampling and allow the network to learn its own variance, we find that the discrete selection process of Top-K fails when in conjunction with stochastic sampling methods. At the noise scale these models are trained upon, vastly different Top-K feature sets (Jaccard 0.075-0.29, chance 0.067) are found on equal model activations due only to the sampling noise, in two forward passes of one trained model on the same token. Soft methods such as JumpReLU fail to hold their sparsity target as well due to sampling, though under different failure modes. Noise moves its achieved sparsity, and at matched sparsity reconstruction fails to track selection stability (r = -0.55). Ablating the KL loss term recovers only 3.9 percent of the lost reconstruction. The rest is due to sampling.

papers.title: GazeVLM: Gaze-Guided Foveated Inference for Efficient Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve remarkable multimodal performance but introduce substantial computational cost due to the large number of visual tokens. Existing approaches typically rely on token pruning, sparse attention, or additional control modules, often introducing accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. This paper presents GazeVLM, a training-free framework that leverages human gaze as a natural guidance signal for efficient inference. GazeVLM allocates computation to gaze-relevant regions through a gaze-guided region-of-interest (ROI) representation and an optional two-scale design that preserves global context. We also construct GazeVLM-VQA, to the best of our knowledge, the first real-world wearable-gaze visual question answering (VQA) dataset specifically constructed for VLM inference, containing reference images, human gaze traces, and gaze-aligned question-answer pairs. Experiments on the GazeVLM-VQA benchmark demonstrate that GazeVLM improves both answer quality and efficiency across Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B and Qwen3-VL-8B models. It reduces visual tokens by up to 84.2%, prefill FLOPs by up to 92.8%, and achieves up to 11.6 times prefill speedup, while improving answer-match accuracy by up to 8.6 percentage points (pp). These results show that aligning VLM computation with human visual attention provides a promising path toward efficient VLM inference. We publicly release the GazeVLM-VQA dataset (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mdi-GezeIkmege3segUQCnvnK6P-skaw?usp=sharing).

papers.title: An elementary proof that linking problems are hard
papers.abstract: We give a new, elementary proof of what we believe is the simplest known example of a "natural" problem in computational 3-dimensional topology that is NP-hard---namely, the Trivial Sublink Problem: given a diagram $L$ of a link in $S^3$ and a positive integer $k$, decide if $L$ contains a $k$ component sublink that is trivial. This problem was previously shown to be NP-hard in independent works of Koenig-Tsvietkova and de Mesmay-Rieck-Sedgwick-Tancer, both of which used reductions from 3SAT. The reduction we describe instead starts with the Independent Set Problem, and allows us to avoid the use of Brunnian links such as the Borromean rings. On the technical level, this entails a new conceptual insight: the Trivial Sublink Problem is hard entirely due to mod 2 pairwise linking, with no need for integral or higher order linking. On the pedagogical level, the reduction we describe is entirely elementary, and thus suitable for introducing undergraduates and non-experts to complexity-theoretic low-dimensional topology.
